a0be44d8165b2df4: RIO DE JANEIRO, Oct 10 — Police in Brazil yesterday rescued 13 children who had been taken hostage in their kindergarten and killed the assailant who threatened to set fire to the building, officials said.
The incident took place in the southern city of Curitiba.

“We successfully neutralised this person and saved the 13 children, who were taken to be checked out and given care by first responders,” the commander of the military police special forces unit in Parana state, Alexandre Lopes Dias, told reporters.
At least one of the children was wounded, he added.
The attacker arrived on a bicycle, jumped the gate at the municipal education centre for young children and barricaded himself into a room with the 13 kindergarteners.
He then spread a flammable substance in the room and held a lighter in his hand. He was carrying a knife and also what was initially believed to be a firearm, but later was found to be fake.
“During the entire negotiation, he stayed with all the children around him and one on his lap,” the police official said.
Talks lasted from 2.5 to three hours. The children became agitated and the attacker started hitting them, Lopes Dias told reporters.

“Once we realised that the kids were becoming increasingly upset, and that the attacker started assaulting them physically, we opted for a tactical intervention to avoid a greater problem,” he explained.
Images shown on local television stations revealed teachers and other school personnel ushering other children out of the facility.
Local media reported that several shots were fired, and heard what sounded like flash bangs.
Police said the assailant had been identified and was schizophrenic. His motive was not immediately clear, nor was it clear if he had ties to anyone at the kindergarten.
“The 13 children are alive and safe!” Curitiba Mayor Eduardo Pimentel wrote on Instagram.
“After anguishing and tense moments, this is the news we were all waiting for.”
Brazil has in recent years experienced multiple attacks on schools. In April 2023, a man killed four children with an ax at a day care in Blumenau, also in southern Brazil. — AFP
ae68f2ae145a9a7f: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Grab aims to increase the earnings of e-hailing drivers and p-hailing delivery partners from 2027 without affecting passenger fares under a proposed minimum earnings framework.
In a statement yesterday, Grab said an agreement in principle had been reached on a proposed minimum baseline rate for e-hailing and p-hailing workers.
“The Gig Consultative Council will continue its deliberations to determine the final rates,” it said.

Grab’s statement follows Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement during the tabling of Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday that the government and Grab would jointly fund a RM160 million package to boost the earnings and welfare of gig workers.
Under the package, median monthly net income for e-hailing drivers is expected to increase by up to RM227, while p-hailing delivery partners’ income is expected to rise by up to RM100.

Grab said other initiatives include a vehicle maintenance subsidy, starting with lubricants, to reduce operating costs by up to 35 per cent, as well as an interim safety incentive to help eligible e-hailing drivers cut regulatory insurance costs by up to 25 per cent.

The company also said its most active drivers and delivery partners would receive 100 per cent coverage for mandatory Social Security Organisation (SOCSO) contributions, while other partners would receive contribution subsidies of up to 50 per cent.
Grab said it will also work with the government to introduce a monthly transit pass offering discounted e-hailing rides to and from train stations, starting in the Klang Valley.

“By offering commuters discounted e-hailing rides to and from train stations, the initiative aims to improve access to fixed route public transportation while generating additional demand for driver-partners,” it said.
Grab executive director Rashid Shukor said improving the livelihoods of its driver and delivery partners remained a priority for the company.
“We understand that every ringgit matters, whether it comes from additional earning opportunities or savings on the everyday costs of working.

“In collaboration with the government, we are taking the lead in the industry to advance measures that can make a meaningful difference to our partners, while building a stronger and more sustainable gig economy,” he added. — Bernama
62f441524e2e42a9: SHAH ALAM: A lorry driver who rammed into 11 vehicles at a traffic light junction in Alam Budiman, Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, yesterday tested positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine.

The collision, involving a 10-tonne lorry and 11 other vehicles at the traffic lights on Jalan Mokhtar Dahari, Section U10, left four people injured, including a 58-year-old man who sustained critical head injuries.
The 51-year-old lorry driver was arrested to assist in investigations after a urine test returned positive for both substances.
Shah Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said the 4.20pm collision involved 12 vehicles, including the 10-tonne lorry.
Based on preliminary investigations, the driver claimed that his vehicle suffered brake failure while travelling downhill from Puncak Perdana towards Puncak Alam, causing him to lose control.
The lorry then crossed into the opposite lane and rammed into 11 vehicles stopped at the traffic lights.
Sarudin said a breathalyser test and a urine test were conducted on the driver, with the latter returning positive for both substances.
He said a 58-year-old man driving a Subaru XV suffered severe head injuries and was receiving treatment in the red zone at Hospital Al-Sultan Abdullah, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), Puncak Alam.
The victim's 53-year-old wife and 17-year-old grandson, who were also in the vehicle, were receiving treatment at the same hospital and were reported to be in stable condition.
Another victim, a 29-year-old Perodua Myvi driver, sustained bodily injuries and was also in stable condition.
The case is being investigated under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Those with information can contact the investigating officer, Inspector Abdul Nasser Peping, at 012-286 3875.
5e319b6d35a5bd81: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Malaysia and Egypt will hold bilateral talks today to review progress in cooperation between the two countries and exchange views on regional and international issues.

In a Facebook post last night, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the meeting with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi would also witness the exchange of several memoranda of understanding between Malaysia and Egypt.

“After tabling the Fifth Madani Budget today, I proceeded directly to the Bunga Raya Complex at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to welcome the arrival of President of the Arab Republic of Egypt Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, who is on a state visit at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
“Welcome to Malaysia, President El-Sisi!” he said.

The Foreign Ministry said in a statement yesterday that El-Sisi was accompanied by Cabinet ministers and senior Egyptian government officials on his first state visit to Malaysia since assuming the presidency in June 2014.
Malaysia and Egypt established diplomatic relations in 1959.
In 2025, Egypt was Malaysia’s seventh-largest trading partner among African countries.

Bilateral trade amounted to RM3.08 billion (US$0.72 billion), with Malaysian exports to Egypt valued at RM2.55 billion (US$0.60 billion) and imports from Egypt totalling RM530 million (US$120 million).
From January to August 2026, total trade between the two countries rose by 74.7 per cent to RM3.49 billion (US$870 million). — Bernama

58258b45b9c70552: PENONOMÉ (Panama), Oct 10 — A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake rocked Panama yesterday, causing buildings and roads to collapse in the center of the country but no immediate reports of casualties.
The shallow tremor was felt across the Central American nation of around 4.5 million people, according to the National Civil Protection System.
It lasted for around a minute.
In Panama City, about 200 kilometres from the epicentre, there were scenes of panic as people rushed to evacuate from the city’s emblematic skyscrapers.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
This aerial view shows people being evacuated at the Hospital del Nino after a severe 7.6 magnitude earthquake hit the country, in Panama City October 9, 2026. — AFP pic

“I was scared because the shaking was very strong and prolonged. Heavy objects like dressers, the bed, and all the kitchen items were shaking,” Salomon Andion, 46, told AFP after evacuating his 15-story building for the second time following aftershocks.
A video widely shared on social media showed water falling from the rooftop pool of a building that’s over 20 stories tall.
Another showed a bridge over the Panama Canal shaking violently but remaining upright as vehicles travelled across it.
“We are facing a major disaster,” President Jose Raul Mulino said, adding that some roads had “completely collapsed.”
“It was horrible, like nothing we ever experienced. My daughter was trapped in school,” Juana Alveo, a 38-year-old cashier at a store in the city of Penonome in central Cocle province told AFP.
The US Geological Survey said the quake struck at 1756 GMT with an epicentre 10 kilometres from the small town of Pitaloza Arriba in central Herrera province.
The USGS initially estimated it to be a magnitude-8.0 quake before revising it to 7.7.
A tsunami warming was issued for the eastern Pacific but later lifted.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

View at the beach after a severe 7.6 magnitude earthquake hit the country, in Santa Catalina, Veraguas province, Panama October 9, 2026. A tsunami warming was issued for the eastern Pacific but later lifted. — AFP pic
The Panama Canal Authority said shipping through the channel, which connects the Pacific and Atlantic oceans, was unaffected and operating “as normal.”
Mulino travelled to Penonome to coordinate the disaster response.
Health Minister Fernando Boyd said the most affected areas were the provinces of Herrera and Cocle as well as Los Santos in the southeast.
He said the town of Tonosi in Los Santos was completely cut off.
“We are trying to figure out how to get there by air, because it’s impossible by land,” he said.
Panama City’s international airport, a major hub for the region, was temporarily closed.
Several flights were diverted to other airports as a precaution, according to the Civil Aeronautics Authority.
The leaders of Colombia, Ecuador and Guatemala all sent messages of solidarity and offers to send aid.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
This view shows a collapsed building and a damaged car after a 7.6-magnitude earthquake struck the country, in Penonome, Panama, on October 9, 2026. — AFP pic
Over 80 aftershocks
Earthquakes are rare in Panama and usually occur in the western Chiriqui province, bordering Costa Rica.
Former president Ricardo Martinelli posted pictures on Instagram of his house in the town of Sona in Veraguas province which collapsed.
A church and a hotel in Penonome also suffered extensive damage, images shared on local media showed.
Over 80 aftershocks, one above magnitude 6.0, were recorded by the local geosciences institute.
Writing on X, Mulino called for calm.
“What happened should not be used to generate alarms and disorder,” he said, adding that he had called for a report on the damage.
The education ministry announced the suspension of classes in schools nationwide.

The Panamanian quake is at least the fourth quake this year in Latin America surpassing 7.0 in magnitude, after devastating back-to-back earthquakes in Venezuela’s Guaira in June and a powerful earthquake in western Colombia in August. — AFP
07229522c9056564: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — The federal government is proposing to introduce a new tax relief of up to RM3,000 for care services provided by confinement centres or qualified individuals after mothers give birth.

In its proposed Budget 2027 tabled in Parliament yesterday, the Finance Ministry also proposed to reclassify or rename the income tax relief of medical treatment into "Health and Well-being", and to keep the existing maximum tax relief for this category at RM10,000.
Under this proposed renamed tax relief category of "Health and Well-being", the ministry proposed to expand it to cover these two expenses, starting from the tax assessment year of 2027:
Tax relief for a maximum RM3,000 in "postnatal care service expenses provided by a confinement centre aor qualified individual";
Tax relief for a maximum RM1,000 for breastfeeding equipment for children aged two and below "paid by self or spouse".
Currently, Malaysian women can already claim a maximum RM1,000 in tax relief when they buy breastfeeding equipment "for own use" for their own children aged two and below.

The difference under the proposed Budget 2027 is that the breastfeeding equipment tax relief will no longer be a separate item of up to RM1,000, but will be merged into or come under the category of "Health and Well-being" which comes with a maximum RM10,000 tax relief.

As of the latest tax relief rules by the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN) for tax assessment year 2025, the RM1,000 tax relief for breastfeeding equipment can only be claimed once in every two years of assessment by a breastfeeding mother who bought it to breastfeed her own child.

Under those existing LHDN rules, the claim must be backed by receipts, and breastfeeding equipment which qualifies are breast pump kit and ice pack; breast milk collection and storage equipment; and cooler set or cooler bag.
Quick refresher on what the existing RM10,000 tax relief for medical treatment expenses covers (You're welcome)
To save you the trouble of checking what is currently covered under the maximum RM10,000 tax relief for medical expenses, it includes:
Serious illness for yourself, your spouse or your child;
Fertility treatment for yourself or your spouse;
Maximum RM1,000 only: Vaccination for yourself, your spouse or your child;
Maximum RM1,000 only: Dental examination and treatment;

Maximum RM1,000 only: Full medical examination; mental health examination or consultation; disease diagnostic test and purchase of self-health monitoring equipment for yourself, your spouse or your child;
For children aged 18 and below: Assessment to diagnose learning disability; early intervention programme or rehabilitation treatment for their learning disability.

b5ddf29122b24421: KUALA LUMPUR: The RM160 million support package for e-hailing and p-hailing workers announced under the 2027 Budget, particularly vehicle insurance assistance, can ease operating costs and boost net income for drivers and riders facing rising premium rates.

Persatuan Rakan Grab Malaysia (PRGM), representing over 20,000 members nationwide, said in a statement that rising insurance premiums were among the earliest issues raised during engagement sessions with Grab Malaysia since its establishment last month.

"Insurance cost assistance under the 2027 Budget is a most welcome development and has the potential to offer meaningful relief to thousands of e-hailing driver partners nationwide," the statement said.

PRGM acknowledged Grab Malaysia's initiative to offer daily insurance payment options to ease drivers' financial pressure, but noted that this focused primarily on payment flexibility and did not fully address overall premium hikes.

The association also welcomed other components in the package, including increased minimum earnings rates, vehicle maintenance assistance, Social Security Organisation contributions, and initiatives to boost demand for e-hailing services.
However, PRGM urged that the implementation mechanism account for operating cost variations by location, service type, and driver needs to ensure benefits are distributed fairly.
The statement added that cooperation between the government and Grab Malaysia is essential to reducing operational costs and improving net income for drivers and riders.

PRGM said it will continue to bridge Grab partners, Grab Malaysia, and the government to ensure ground-level feedback and challenges faced by gig workers are addressed through constructive engagement.
The association expressed hope for stronger collaboration with Grab Malaysia, particularly on issues directly impacting earnings, operating costs, and the welfare of drivers and riders.

"For PRGM, the success of any policy lies not just in the allocated sum announced, but in how meaningfully the benefits are felt by drivers and delivery partners working daily to support their families," it said.
1810c6b75597fc42: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 10 — An artificial intelligence model developed by Anthropic submitted a fabricated tip about an unsolved homicide to Philadelphia police, authorities said yesterday, criticising the company for taking two months to report the incident.
The Philadelphia Police Department said the false submission was made in July through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, a public website where people can share information about unsolved killings.

According to Anthropic’s account, as relayed by police, the model was running a test that involved interacting with randomly selected websites when it reached the site and filed false information about an unsolved murder.
The AI model presented itself as someone who might have knowledge of the case.

The incident echoed other recent cases of unintended behaviour involving AI models, including one where an OpenAI agent undergoing a security evaluation broke out of its testing environment and breached systems at AI platform Hugging Face.
The episode heightened concerns about the AI industry’s increased use of AI agents, systems programmed to take multi-step actions without human supervision.
Anthropic published a report yesterday outlining multiple types of “unintended” actions that its models have taken, including the incident involving the Philadelphia Police Department website.
Other organisations impacted included the White House and other US government agencies, the report said.
The newly revealed incidents “had minimal real-world impact” and were “significantly less severe” than other cybersecurity incidents previously reported, Anthropic said.

The company outlined four categories of incidents that it found during an internal review of its Claude model: exploiting “basic” coding flaws, submitting forms on websites, bypassing requirements for tokens or fees, and using short URLs to get around other limits.

Anthropic has turned off internet access for Claude during all internal testing for now “until we have confirmed that our security and monitoring measures... reliably catch behaviours like these,” the report said.
Philadelphia police said the phony tip, dated July 18, was flagged as spam and never reached the department’s Real-Time Crime Centre for vetting.
They added that there was no sign that police systems had been breached or department data compromised.
Anthropic discovered the incident on September 28, shut down the automated testing process responsible and added a new validation step for future tests, police said.
The company alerted the department on October 7, and the two sides met the following day.
“The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the City is unacceptable,” the department said.

Police said their safeguards had limited the impact, but that these “do not diminish the seriousness of an AI system presenting fabricated information as though it came from a person with knowledge of a homicide.”
“Unsolved cases involve real victims, grieving families and investigators working to secure answers,” the statement added. — AFP
aba8baba35300b66: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has been directed to review data on homeless people in the city centre collected through enforcement operations over the past three years.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the review was aimed at identifying the best solutions to address homelessness in the city centre.
She also wants to seek input from non-governmental organisations (NGOs) working on the ground before bringing any proposed measures to the Cabinet.
"I do not want us to simply keep repeating enforcement operations against homeless people.
"I want us to improve the system so that those who need help do not keep returning to the streets," she said in a statement last night.
On Tuesday, Yeoh, who is also the Segambut member of parliament, joined the KL Strike operation in Kuala Lumpur, involving DBKL, the Social Welfare Department and other relevant agencies.
She acknowledged that homelessness could persist if adequate follow-up support was not provided after individuals were screened and referred to the relevant agencies.
"How long are we going to keep carrying out the same homeless outreach operations if they eventually return to the streets?

"I have seen the challenges on the ground myself. Screening facilities are limited, some people lack identification documents and require mental health treatment, while senior citizens and children need protection," she said.
a83116afa842dd3a: WASHINGTON, Oct 10 — Condemnation of US plans for a public execution by military firing squad escalated yesterday, as Vice President JD Vance cast doubt on whether it would be livestreamed as proposed and insisted he would not watch if it is.
Nidal Hasan’s execution — scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by US military firing squad since 1945.
Asked about the planned livestream, Vance told journalists he does not “know that that’s actually going to happen.”

“This is a guy who committed, in my view, the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside of 9/11,” Vance said, but added that if the execution is broadcast live, “I’m not going to be watching it.”
Representative Austin Scott of President Donald Trump’s Republican Party said he supported executing Hasan but “livestreaming executions is what jihadists do. America is better than that.”

Senator Mark Kelly, a Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, said Hasan should “face justice” but that public executions are “the kind of thing Iran and the Taliban do. Is this who we want to be associated with?”
A Pentagon official told AFP on Thursday that the execution would be streamed live, after US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said “we’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public.”
But Trump yesterday contradicted Hegseth’s confirmation, and said there has been no decision yet on whether to publicly broadcast the execution, which he supports.
“They are making a determination about that, but he will be killed,” Trump said. “I really don’t care how he goes, as long as he goes.”
Tech firms YouTube, Meta and X did not immediately respond to requests for comment on whether they would allow the execution to be streamed on their platforms.
TikTok directed AFP to its policy banning depictions of “graphic incidents and violence” including “the shooting of an individual.”

The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights condemned the move, saying in a message sent to AFP yesterday that “the livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture.”
Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, said it was a “barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered.”
‘Compound the cruelty’
Hegseth said it would be the military’s first firing squad execution since World War II.
“People need to understand that... there’s serious consequence for these types of things,” Hegseth said in a video shared Thursday on official Pentagon X accounts.
The last US military execution was carried out in 1961, when John Bennett was hanged for rape and attempted murder.
The Death Penalty Information Centre says 135 troops have been executed by the US military since 1916.
According to rights group Amnesty International, at least 17 public executions are known to have been carried out in 2025 — six in Afghanistan and 11 in Iran.
Amnesty’s Justin Mazzola said Friday that the death penalty is “a violation of human rights,” and that streaming Hasan’s execution “would only compound the cruelty.”
Twelve of the 13 people Hasan killed and 30 of those he wounded were soldiers. He was shot by a civilian police officer who responded to the attack and is paralysed from the waist down.
Hasan chose to conduct his own defence during the trial but called no witnesses and gave no testimony, and made no attempt to deny the charges.
He was sentenced to death by a military jury in 2013.
Court-appointed defence attorneys expressed concern that he was seeking execution.

The court that convicted Hasan was told he was opposed to the US military’s occupations of Iraq and Afghanistan, and that he had spoken online with an alleged Al-Qaeda figure, radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki, an American citizen subsequently killed in a US drone strike in Yemen. — AFP
057ecea8ee42e820: KUALA LUMPUR: A simple wave from a boy to a passing Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) train in Kempas, Johor, warmed hearts online after the driver returned the greeting with a wave and a honk.
The moment, captured on video and shared on Threads by the boy's mother, user @_zrily, showed her son waving at the passing train before the driver responded.
Delighted by the gesture, she took to social media to thank the driver for making her son's day.
"Who was the man driving the train near Kempas at 6.30pm earlier? Thank you so much for making my child so happy today," she wrote.
The video has since garnered more than 92,000 views and 5,000 likes, drawing smiles from social media users.
The exchange even caught the attention of KTMB, which responded to the post through its official Threads account.
"Thank you for sharing this adorable moment. Your child's smile and happiness are our happiness too," it said.
The video also sparked a wave of nostalgia among social media users, many of whom recalled their childhood days of waving at passing trains.
Several reminisced about a time when trains were a familiar sight in their neighbourhoods and waving to locomotive drivers was a simple childhood pleasure.
Others were pleased to see the tradition continuing with a new generation of children.

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — One of my favourite discoveries during my visit to Seoul many years ago was a seasonal Korean café beverage called goguma latte (고구마 라떼).

Goguma (Korean for sweet potato) is especially popular during the colder months. Roasted sweet potatoes are sold as a winter snack while cafés have creatively transformed the humble tuber into the aforementioned drink.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Uncooked sweet potatoes. — Picture by CK Lim
Essentially steamed sweet potato blended with milk or soy milk, goguma latte is naturally sweet and comforting.
I’ve decided to put my own spin on this, albeit via a slightly different route. Instead of dairy milk, how about fresh, homemade soy milk?
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Raw organic soybeans. — Picture by CK Lim
The soy milk (known as doujiang in Mandarin) provides a familiar nutty flavour and naturally creamy body, which matches the mellow sweetness of the sweet potatoes perfectly.
Then there is the luxurious, lavender hue of the sweet potato soy milk (I’ve used purple sweet potatoes specifically for this effect), which simply whispers “cosy”, no?
SWEET POTATO SOY MILK
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Cups of frothy, lavender-hued soy milk. — Picture by CK Lim
There are, naturally, more straightforward ways to make soy milk. So consider my approach more of an infusion... or fusion, as it were.

Even then, most recipes suggest blending the soy milk with the additional ingredient. This is easier, of course, but I find the result a tad clumpy as all the fibre is still retained in the blended milk.
How I do this differently is to blend the soaked raw soybeans with the cooked sweet potato before straining everything together.
Yes, this is an extra step but it means the finished sweet potato soy milk is silky smooth and creamy without any sludge.
Speaking of “sludge”, let’s not forget the leftover pulp. Don’t throw it away!
Because the soy beans and sweet potato are blended together, the douzha (literally “bean dregs” in Mandarin) is highly nutritious. Plenty of soy protein and fibre from the sweet potatoes.

Me, I like stirring the douzha into my morning oats as it cooks (the soybean pulp is still raw, remember, so you still have to cook it). It thickens the oats naturally and adds a mild sweet potato flavour.
Note that I’ve added no sugar as the natural sugars and starches from the sweet potato give the blended soy milk a gentler, less cloying sweetness.
Ingredients
100 g dried organic soybeans
2 medium purple sweet potatoes
1.2 litres filtered water
Method
Rinse the dried organic soybeans thoroughly. Place them in a large bowl and cover with plenty of water.
Soak the beans overnight until fully rehydrated. Drain and rinse well.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Soak the soybeans overnight. — Picture by CK Lim
Steam the sweet potatoes for about 12 to 15 minutes, or until a fork slides easily through their centres. Allow it to cool slightly.
Transfer the soaked soybeans and steamed sweet potatoes to a blender. Pour in the filtered water and blend on high for about 2 minutes, or until the mixture is smooth and milky.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Blend the steamed sweet potatoes and soaked soybeans together. — Picture by CK Lim
Drape a muslin cloth or cheesecloth over a large cooking pot. Pour the blended mixture into the cloth.
Collecting the ends of the cloth together, squeeze firmly to extract as much of the liquid as possible. Continue squeezing until the pulp remaining in the cloth feels relatively dry.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Strain the blended mixture through a muslin cloth or cheesecloth. — Picture by CK Lim
Place the pot over medium-low heat. Stir continuously, making sure to scrape the bottom of the pot to prevent the sweet potato starch from settling and burning.
Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer. Once simmering, reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, stirring regularly. This cooks the soybeans thoroughly and removes any raw bean flavour.
Remove from the heat and pour directly into cups. Best served warm.

23c6daf64509b395: When news of the Aug 26 Nepal glacial and flood disaster broke, Dr Manivannan Rethinam’s first thoughts went out to his sister Komathi who was on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash.
Together with her husband, he tried but failed to reach her. She is among 54 Malaysians still listed as missing. No one knows if they are still alive, and that is the problem.
Since then, Manivannan, who heads the Malaysian Solidarity Families in Hope support group dealing with the authorities, has learned a brutal truth: there is no sympathy in bureaucracy or the law.
Without a death certificate, spouses and children have no access to joint bank accounts or the victim’s EPF savings. They cannot sell family homes nor cancel hire purchase contracts.
All the banks can do is express sympathy for their loss. Without a death certificate, they cannot act, and without a body identified through DNA, a death certificate cannot be issued.
The DNA dilemma
And herein lies the cruellest of ironies: the bodies may never be found.
Nepalese rescue teams have spent weeks searching, but the terrain is treacherous and inaccessible. Officials have privately admitted that finding all 54 bodies is “unlikely”.

Insurance companies, meanwhile, cannot pay out on life policies. Their position is legally defensible: without a death certificate, there is no confirmation of death. DNA identification requires a body. No body means no DNA. No DNA, no death certificate. No death certificate, no payout.
This Catch-22 situation is driving the affected families to despair.

Compounding the agony is the legal inconsistency between Malaysia and Nepal. Under Malaysian law, a person can legally be declared dead only after being missing for seven years. In Nepal, it takes only three years.
The question is which jurisdiction takes precedence. The answer, according to Malaysian legal experts, is murky.
Those missing are Malaysian citizens, so Malaysian law governs their estates. But the deaths occurred on Nepalese soil. The question of jurisdiction may take years to resolve in courts.
According to Manivannan the Malaysian embassy in Kathmandu has agreed to accept Nepal’s jurisdiction over this, but that is only a verbal assurance.
For one person, the pain has taken a particularly bitter form.
His wife had bought a new car just months before she left for Nepal. Now the husband faces an impossible choice.
He cannot afford the monthly instalments on his own, along with the mortgage and his children’s expenses. He decided to return the car to the bank, surrendering it to stop the bleeding.
But the bank’s response was clinical. They asked him to stop payments for three months, and they will repossess the vehicle.
But that raises another problem — he will be liable for the default penalty, the repossession charges, and any shortfall between the auction price and the outstanding loan balance.
Information blackout
Perhaps most agonising of all is the silence.

The missing person’s next-of-kin cannot obtain any information about their loved one’s financial accounts. Bank Negara has strict confidentiality laws that prevent banks from disclosing account details to family members without a power of attorney or a court order.
But how do you get a power of attorney from a person who is missing?

Manivannan says the families are unable to get the August salary of their breadwinners who are missing because employers can only deposit the money in the missing person’s bank account. “Employers cannot release it to the next-of-kin,” he pointed out.
For some families, the tragedy is almost too vast to comprehend.

The credit cards of those missing are still active, and utility bills must still be paid. Worse than that insurance companies may kickstart automatic premium loan to keep policies alive although the insured may eventually be declared dead.
It is a technicality that the Life Insurance Association of Malaysia and Bank Negara must quickly resolve to prevent more financial losses.
Calls for Bank Negara to step in
Families and advocates now want Bank Negara to intervene.

“We need Bank Negara to issue a directive to all financial institutions: freeze all payments, waive all penalties, suspend all repossessions, and allow next-of-kin access to accounts based on a police report of the disappearance — not a death certificate,” says Manivannan.
More needs to be done. The government must consider emergency legislative measures to address the seven-year rule in exceptional disaster situations.

There must also be mechanisms for insurance companies and financial institutions to provide appropriate interim assistance to affected families while the legal status of their loved ones remains unresolved.

Behind every legal argument, every bureaucratic hurdle, every frozen account, there is a human being — a wife who cannot sleep, a child who cannot concentrate at school, a parent who cannot stop crying.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
e71e91d6d3d5cda1: PETALING JAYA: When Mala Davi walked into her daughter’s apartment in 2011, she barely recognised her. The 19-year-old Vishalatchi Arunagiri weighed just 26kg. That was the physical toll of living with severe mental distress over a prolonged period.
Soon after, Visha was diagnosed with schizophrenia, which changed the course of her life forever.
After receiving treatment and learning to manage her condition, Visha founded Suara Minda, a mental health NGO she now runs with her mother.
The organisation, founded in 2020, focuses on advocacy, offering activities that support wellbeing and creating a safe space for those from underprivileged backgrounds.
But getting there was far from straightforward.

“I left Malaysia when I was five and lived in Thailand for 14 years. I was diagnosed with a learning disability and went to a special needs school before being home-schooled,” Visha, 34, told FMT Lifestyle.

She returned to Malaysia to pursue fashion merchandising. However, when the course proved overwhelming for her, and problems at home added to her stress, she fell into a depression, started drinking, and began smoking.

Her mother, meanwhile, had no idea how serious her daughter's situation had become. Although Visha had been staying with friends and relatives, she was left alone for three weeks, during which her symptoms first emerged. By the time Mala travelled from Thailand to see her, Visha was in crisis mode.
“Her nails were black, the house was in a bad state, and she was talking and laughing to herself at midnight, standing at the door,” Mala recalled.
“At first, I thought I was psychic because I could hear voices and predict things. Eventually, I realised the voices were lying to me," Visha said.

A psychiatrist diagnosed her with schizophrenia. “The psychiatrist was shocked when she saw that Visha weighed 26kg. The doctor said she might not have survived if we had delayed getting help,” Mala said.
Visha initially resisted treatment and medication but eventually agreed after persuasion from her family, undergoing psychotherapy and a three-month rehabilitation programme.
By 2014, she was doing much better. For Mala, the experience also changed how she viewed her daughter.

“I saw her as Visha, not as a schizophrenic. Eventually, I stopped being the overthinking mother and became a caregiver and facilitator. In 2011, there wasn’t much awareness about support groups. A lot of people still don’t know these places exist.”

Both mother and daughter became actively involved with the Malaysian Mental Health Association (MMHA) in 2014, while Mala also became a caregiver education trainer and trained in Mental Health First Aid.
Eventually, they created their own platform, “Suara Minda”, which means “Mind Voice”.
The NGO operates on a peer-run model, where individuals who have undergone psychiatric rehabilitation help guide others through early support and recovery.
It also runs creative workshops for people of all ages, from children to senior citizens, featuring activities such as pottery making, flower arrangement, baking, and stone art.

“I started doing creative activities because I saw the difference they made in me,” Visha said. “They help me focus, reduce my anxiety and, sometimes, make the voices less disturbing when I’m doing something with my hands.”
Last year alone, Suara Minda conducted 20 workshops and awareness talks with B40 communities, where Visha shared her lived experience while Mala spoke from her perspective as a caregiver.
“There are still so many myths, including the idea that people with schizophrenia are automatically dangerous or violent. When people hear Visha’s story, they’re usually surprised,” she said.
Visha still hears voices and has faced setbacks, including a hospital admission three years ago after becoming suicidal. She said she is now doing well under the care of her psychiatrist.
“Building Suara Minda has been a struggle. I still have to respect my limits and make time to rest. But this work gives me a sense of purpose and an opportunity to contribute,” she said.
Her goal now is to grow the NGO, and make counselling and psychotherapy more accessible.
“Suara Minda is a safe, non-judgemental place. Just come for a coffee and share what you’re going through when you have nobody else to talk to,” Mala said.
Follow Suara Minda on Facebook and contact Mala Davi at 017-350 3257.
e85697e3117ad6f6: PETALING JAYA: Hubungan lama antara Setiausaha Agung Bersatu Azmin Ali dan Menteri Besar Selangor Amirudin Shari dilihat mampu memudahkan kerjasama antara kerajaan negeri dengan Adun parti itu, kata penganalisis.

Mazlan Ali daripada Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) berkata, keakraban kedua-dua pemimpin sejak bersama dalam PKR boleh membantu melancarkan rundingan perjanjian kerjasama yang dijangka melibatkan sokongan wakil rakyat pembangkang terhadap pentadbiran negeri.

“Dulu kita kenal Azmin dan Amirudin cukup akrab jadi pada saya hubungan baik antara Azmin dan Amirudin ni akan menjayakan bentuk kerjasama dan akan jadi fasa baru dalam politik negeri Selangor,” katanya kepada FMT.
Beliau mengulas rundingan antara kerajaan Selangor dengan Adun Bersatu mengenai perjanjian kerjasama yang dijangka melibatkan sokongan wakil rakyat pembangkang terhadap pentadbiran negeri.
Amirudin pada Khamis berkata, rundingan mengenai terma perjanjian masih berjalan dan berharap persetujuan dapat dimeterai sebelum pembentangan Belanjawan Selangor 2027 bulan depan.
Naib presiden PKR itu yang juga pengarah strategi pilihan raya Pakatan Harapan (PH) turut memaklumkan setakat ini tiada permintaan luar biasa dikemukakan sepanjang rundingan.
Bagaimanapun, Adun Permatang Nurul Syazwani Noh mendakwa beliau tidak dimaklumkan mengenai rundingan yang dikatakan sudah sampai ke peringkat memuktamadkan terma perjanjian.
Ketika ini, PH memiliki 32 daripada 56 DUN Selangor manakala Barisan Nasional (BN) dua kerusi. Kedua-duanya memnbentuk kerajaan negeri selepas PRN 2023.
Pembangkang pula menguasai 21 kerusi terdiri Bersatu (11) dan PAS (10) sementara seorang Adun bebas menyokong kerajaan negeri.
Untuk rekod, Azmin dan Amirudin pernah menjadi sekutu rapat dalam PKR, dengan Amirudin berkhidmat sebagai exco negeri ketika Azmin menjadi menteri besar Selangor.
Amirudin kemudian menggantikan Azmin sebagai menteri besar pada Jun 2018 selepas pemimpin itu dilantik sebagai menteri hal ehwal ekonomi dalam Kabinet persekutuan.
Azmin pernah menyifatkan Amirudin sebagai anak didiknya dan mendakwa beliau mencadangkan nama Amirudin untuk dipertimbangkan sebagai penggantinya.
Hubungan politik kedua-duanya berubah selepas Azmin dipecat PKR dan menyertai Bersatu pada 2020 ketika 'Langkah Sheraton', menyaksikan pentadbiran PH 1.0 terkubur.

Persaingan mereka semakin ketara apabila Amirudin menewaskan Azmin di Parlimen Gombak pada PRU15, namun hubungan peribadi kedua-duanya dilihat masih baik apabila Azmin memanggil Amirudin sebagai 'adinda' ketika berbahas di DUN Selangor pada Ogos lalu.
Menurut Mazlan, kedudukan Bersatu di Selangor menjadikan kerjasama itu signifikan, terutama jika wakil rakyat parti berkenaan menyokong kerajaan negeri dalam urusan belanjawan.
Beliau turut melihat langkah itu sebagai strategi Bersatu ketika hubungannya dengan PAS semakin renggang.
"Ia berpotensi mengubah percaturan politik Selangor dalam menghadapi kemungkinan kerjasama BN-PAS pada pilihan raya akan datang" katanya.

Syaza Shukri daripada Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia (UIAM) pula berkata, peluang kerjasama PH-Bersatu lebih cerah di Selangor berbanding Melaka, mengambil kira hubungan antara pemimpin serta kedudukan Bersatu di negeri itu.
Katanya, kerjasama itu pada peringkat awal lebih menyerupai memorandum persefahaman (MoU) atau perjanjian keyakinan dan perbekalan (CSA), yang boleh membantu menjamin kestabilan pentadbiran Amirudin.

Beliau berkata, perkembangan itu juga berpotensi menjadi langkah awal untuk PH dan Bersatu menghadapi kemungkinan cabaran BN-PAS, sebelum diterjemahkan kepada kerjasama lebih luas di peringkat nasional.
“Jika tiada halangan besar, kerjasama ini boleh berkembang menjadi kerjasama politik menjelang PRU,” katanya.
75f9a141edbf783b: RANCHI, (India): Skipper Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford struck blazing knocks as the West Indies recorded the second-highest T20 chase of all time on Friday to beat India by six wickets.

After India posted 249-5 batting first, the West Indies rode on a 120-run fourth-wicket partnership between Hope, who hit an unbeaten 102, and Rutherford (84) to achieve the target with nine balls to spare in Ranchi.
Hope completed the win with the ninth six of his innings and one that brought up his century off 45 balls, as the West Indies bounced back to level the five-match series at 1-1.
"When you chase here in India, you always give yourself a chance," said Hope.
"You always think you're in the game, regardless of what score is on the board. But (from) 5-2 was always going to be challenging."
South Africa hold the record for the highest successful run chase in men's T20 cricket, scoring 259-4 against the West Indies in Centurion in 2023.
West Indies' previous best chase was when they overhauled 231 by South Africa in Johannesburg in 2015.
Hope and the left-handed Rutherford led an aggressive counter-attack after joining forces with the West Indies 58-3.
Rutherford reached his fifty off 24 balls and kept up the charge before falling to left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav.
He hit seven fours and seven sixes in his 37-ball blitz.
Hope, who struck his second T20 ton, stood firm and put on an unbeaten stand of 74 with Romario Shepherd, who hit 34.
Rutherford later called Hope a "phenomenal player" and one who "inspires" him.
Indian speedster Mayank Yadav struck in the opening over with two successive wickets, including removing Shimron Hetmyer for a first-ball duck.
Yadav also bowled Rovman Powell for 24 with a delivery that clocked 150 km/h (93 mph), but Hope and Rutherford turned the match in the West Indies' favour.
Earlier, Sanju Samson made 82 off 41 balls before skipper Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma powered India to an imposing total after being asked to bat first.
Iyer said dew played a major part in the West Indies chase.
"The margin of error on this wicket was very minor. Any minor error was going into the stands," he said.
Samson and Ishan Kishan (43) put on 97 runs for the second wicket after swashbuckling opener Abhishek Sharma departed for 20.
Spinner Roston Chase struck the first blow and then delivered two more — bowling Kishan and Shivam Dube — to check India's surge.
Pace bowler Shamar Springer dismissed Samson but Iyer and Varma bludgeoned 83 runs off 33 balls for the fifth wicket.
Iyer fell to the penultimate ball of the innings after a rapid 40 off 18 balls while Varma finished unbeaten with 44 in equally quick time.
The third match is on Sunday in Indore. — AFP

a77ff2682dfd0582: KUALA LUMPUR: Batu Pahat recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 190 as of 8am today, as worsening haze affected several areas in Johor and Negri Sembilan.
According to data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Larkin, Pasir Gudang, and Tangkak recorded an API of 185.
Seremban registered an API of 184, followed by Segamat at 181 and Nilai at 180.
As of 8am, 32 locations nationwide recorded unhealthy API readings, while 36 showed moderate air quality. No locations recorded good or hazardous air quality.
In the Klang Valley, at least nine locations, including Putrajaya, Cheras, and Shah Alam, recorded unhealthy API levels above 101.
The worsening conditions prompted authorities to implement precautionary measures, including school closures in severely affected areas.
The current haze episode is linked to forest and peatland fires in neighbouring Indonesia, where dry weather has accelerated the spread of fire and smoke across the region.
Malaysia and Indonesia are stepping up cooperation to tackle transboundary haze through hotspot monitoring, enforcement against open burning, and enhanced firefighting measures.
Both nations have also discussed potential cloud-seeding operations and resource-sharing, with Malaysia continuing to engage Indonesia and other Asean members on the recurring issue.
The haze remains a recurring regional environmental problem during prolonged dry spells, when smoke from Indonesian land fires drifts across national borders.
Malaysia continues to monitor air quality through APIMS, issue health advisories, and coordinate agency responses when API readings reach unhealthy levels.
The Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution, adopted in 2002, serves as the regional framework for member states to prevent, monitor, and mitigate land and forest fires.

8b87953e47ea20e4: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump asked the US Supreme Court on Friday to revive his dismissed lawsuit against his 2016 Democratic rival Hillary Clinton accusing her of conspiring along with former FBI Director James Comey and others to rig that year's election by linking his campaign to Russia.

The Republican president filed his appeal after a federal judge threw out the case and imposed nearly US$1 million in sanctions against Trump and one of his lawyers for bringing a "frivolous" suit. A US appeals court subsequently upheld the dismissal and sanctions.

Trump's lawyers wrote in the appeal that Supreme Court review of the case is needed in order to protect the presidency. They wrote that the decisions by the lower courts reflect "a deeply troubling trend of federal courts using sanctions and disciplinary threats to punish the president and his lawyers for legitimate legal positions that those courts (erroneously) reject."

In 2022, when he was out of office after losing the 2020 election, Trump sued Clinton, Comey, former British intelligence officer Christopher Steele, the Democratic National Committee and numerous others in a lengthy complaint filed in federal court in Florida.

Trump, who has a history of suing adversaries, alleged that in the lead-up to the 2016 election, Clinton conspired with allies to discredit him with a "false narrative" that he and his campaign colluded with Russia. The lengthy suit alleged "racketeering" and a "conspiracy to commit injurious falsehood," among other claims.
Trump defeated Clinton in that election, despite losing the national popular vote, and served his first term in office from 2017 to 2021.

US government officials have accused Russia of meddling in the 2016 election, and an investigation led by former FBI chief Robert Mueller documented extensive contacts between members of the Trump campaign and Russian operatives who sought to influence the election in his favor. Trump has called the idea of Russian interference a "hoax".

Since losing to Democrat Joe Biden in 2020, Trump has made false claims of widespread voting fraud in that year's election. Trump regained the presidency by defeating Democrat Kamala Harris in 2024, and has continued to make those false claims.
'Political manifesto'

US District Judge Donald Middlebrooks dismissed Trump's lawsuit against Clinton, citing numerous inadequacies, including that Trump waited too long to bring some of the claims. The judge likened Trump's lawsuit to a "two-hundred-page political manifesto outlining his grievances against those that have opposed him."

Middlebrooks later ordered Trump and his lead attorney in the case, Alina Habba, to pay nearly US$1 million in fees and costs, imposing the sanctions for bringing a case that the judge said was intended "to dishonestly advance a political narrative." The judge also faulted Trump and his lawyers for a "continuing pattern of misuse of the courts".
Middlebrooks found that the lawsuit used abusive litigation tactics, contained "knowingly false" factual allegations and asserted "frivolous" legal theories.
The Atlanta-based 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the judge's rulings in 2025, including the sanctions.
"Many of Trump's and Habba's legal arguments were indeed frivolous," the 11th Circuit stated.

In Friday's filing, lawyers for Trump and Habba said the time limit for filing the lawsuit should have been extended because he chose to defer suing during his first term in office in order to carry out his constitutional responsibilities as president.
"This court's intervention is necessary to protect the presidency, and to prevent judicial disagreement from becoming a license to punish its advocates," the filing stated.

Mueller, serving as a special counsel appointed by the justice department, issued a 2019 report on his investigation. The report stated that Russia "interfered in the 2016 presidential election in sweeping and systematic fashion," but also stated that "the investigation did not establish that members of the Trump campaign conspired or coordinated with the Russian government in its election interference activities."
Mueller said in his report that he found "numerous links" and that the Trump campaign "expected it would benefit" from Russia's effort to tilt the election in Trump's favor.
Trump's then-Attorney General William Barr appointed a different special counsel, John Durham, in 2019 to look into potential missteps by the FBI.

In a 2023 report, Durham concluded that the FBI lacked "actual evidence" to investigate Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and relied too heavily on tips provided by Trump's political opponents to fuel the probe.

Trump's justice department last year indicted Comey, one of several adversaries of the president hit with criminal charges, accusing him of making false statements and obstructing Congress after he was accused of lying about authorizing leaks to the news media. A federal judge subsequently dismissed the indictment, finding that the prosecutor who Trump handpicked to prosecute Comey had been unlawfully appointed.

Steele, working for an opposition research firm that was hired by a law firm on behalf of the Clinton campaign and the Democratic National Committee, produced a dossier that alleged ties between Trump's campaign and Russia as well as other salacious accusations, all of which Trump denied.
f24316aa3e978c46: KUALA LUMPUR: Nearly two months after losing contact with her husband following the floods disaster in Nepal, Hani Othman remains hopeful that Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa will return to his family.
In a Facebook post today, Hani shared that her husband, better known as Loe, had appeared in her dreams three times, expressing his wish to return home.

Fakhrul Munir was reported missing after the four-wheel drive vehicle carrying his group on an expedition to Everest Base Camp via the Tibet route was believed to have been hit by severe floods and landslides in the Rasuwa valley.

"So he decided not to proceed even though he really wanted to reach the peak, because he had promised his family to return safely.
"But things turned out differently on this trip to Nepal," she said.
bc6a8767880817b5: PETALING JAYA: Tawaran kerajaan untuk menambah jawatan tetap bagi doktor kontrak perlu disertai langkah meningkatkan pengekalan mereka dalam sistem kesihatan awam, kata seorang penyelidik kesihatan awam.

Ilyana Mukhriz, pegawai penyelidik di Institut Penyelidikan Khazanah (KRI), berkata pelantikan tetap sahaja tidak akan menyelesaikan cabaran mengekalkan doktor dalam sistem kesihatan awam, meskipun ia merupakan langkah penting untuk meningkatkan jaminan pekerjaan.

“Peruntukan belanjawan sahaja tidak dapat menyelesaikan semua masalah. Namun, langkah seterusnya perlu memastikan doktor mempunyai keadaan kerja yang baik, komunikasi yang jelas mengenai peluang perkembangan kerjaya, jawatan kanan tetap yang lebih mencukupi menerusi pewujudan jawatan berdasarkan kluster dan merit, serta imbuhan yang adil,” katanya kepada FMT.
Beliau berkata doktor yang ditempatkan di kawasan luar bandar juga perlu diberikan kuarters kediaman, kemudahan rehat dan akses kepada keperluan asas yang mencukupi.

Menerusi pembentangan Belanjawan 2027 semalam, kerajaan mengumumkan lebih 9,000 doktor kontrak akan ditawarkan jawatan tetap tahun depan. Doktor yang berjaya menamatkan latihan siswazah juga akan ditawarkan pelantikan tetap sebagai pegawai perubatan.

Bagaimanapun, Ilyana berkata sebelum ini terdapat doktor yang tidak melapor diri untuk bertugas walaupun sudah menerima tawaran jawatan tetap. Minggu lalu, Menteri Kesihatan Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad berkata hanya 63% pegawai perubatan yang ditawarkan penempatan tetap di Sabah dan Sarawak tahun ini telah melapor diri.

Dalam pada itu, Ilyana berkata Belanjawan 2027 sepatutnya memberikan penekanan lebih besar kepada usaha mencegah penyakit kronik melalui pendidikan dan program yang menggalakkan perubahan tingkah laku.
“Jika kita tidak menangani peningkatan penyakit kronik, kita akhirnya akan membelanjakan lebih banyak wang pada masa depan untuk menyediakan rawatan bagi menyembuhkan penyakit.”

Beliau turut menggesa penambahbaikan dalam proses perolehan dan penyelenggaraan peralatan perubatan. Katanya, sesetengah aset hospital tidak lagi dapat dibaiki walaupun lebih RM770 juta diperuntukkan untuk peralatan baharu.

Pusat Galen untuk Dasar Kesihatan dan Sosial berkata penukaran jawatan doktor kontrak sedia ada kepada jawatan tetap tidak semestinya meningkatkan bilangan petugas kesihatan yang memberikan perkhidmatan.

Ketua Pegawai Eksekutifnya, Azrul Khalib, menggesa pelaksanaan program pengambilan dan pengekalan petugas kesihatan yang dibiayai untuk tempoh beberapa tahun, serta penubuhan suruhanjaya perkhidmatan kesihatan bebas bagi menambah baik pengambilan, penempatan, imbuhan dan perkembangan kerjaya.

Beliau berkata Belanjawan 2027 telah melepaskan peluang untuk melaksanakan reformasi struktur dalam sektor kesihatan kerana peningkatan perbelanjaan semata-mata tidak akan menyelesaikan masalah yang membelenggu sistem itu.

“Belanjawan ini memberikan kelegaan dalam beberapa bidang penting. Bagaimanapun, ia mengelak daripada membuat keputusan sukar yang diperlukan untuk memastikan perkhidmatan kesihatan mampan, mampu dibiayai dan mudah diakses dalam tempoh sedekad akan datang,” katanya.
Belanjawan 2027 memperuntukkan RM47 bilion kepada Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM), sedikit meningkat berbanding RM46 bilion pada 2026.

Langkah lain termasuk peruntukan lebih RM770 juta bagi peralatan perubatan moden, RM200 juta untuk penyumberan luar rawatan pesakit ke hospital lain bagi mengurangkan tempoh menunggu, RM1.2 bilion untuk penyelenggaraan kemudahan kesihatan awam, pengenalan skim insurans perubatan MediAsas serta pelaksanaan rekod perubatan elektronik di seluruh negara.
dabf90d924360175: LIVERPOOL: Manchester City will face the full fury of Anfield on Sunday when the Premier League leaders confront old rivals Liverpool in their first game since being found guilty of breaking financial rules.

City can expect a hostile reception from Liverpool fans after an independent commission found they arranged "sham" deals to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million (US$1.2 billion) between 2009 and 2018.

The financial breaches occurred during a period in which City won three Premier League titles and numerous other trophies, with Liverpool struggling to break the Etihad Stadium outfit's silverware monopoly.
City have appealed against the devastating verdict and manager Enzo Maresca was bullish on Friday that they will overturn the original ruling.
But the Premier League season is now stuck in stasis awaiting a ruling on the appeal and any potential sanction.
"I think the worst thing probably is the uncertainty, that no one knows what's going to happen," Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said on Friday.
A severe points penalty leading to relegation or even expulsion from the English top flight are on the table, while there is also speculation City could be stripped of titles.
"I think they have to be stripped of the titles. Otherwise you send the wrong message to anyone in the future," John Gibbons of Liverpool podcast The Anfield Wrap told AFP.
"There can't be any trust now, certainly not if there's not an admission of guilt. For me, I don't see how Manchester City continue in the league."
Over the past 12 years, Liverpool have finished second to City on three occasions.
Only one of those in 2013/14 came during the period under scrutiny.
But City's rivals believe the wrongdoing in that period built the foundations for a golden era under former boss Pep Guardiola, who stepped down at the end of last season.
'Not playing by same rules'
Twice Jurgen Klopp's Reds missed out on the title despite amassing over 90 points.
Those title battles turned meetings between City and Liverpool into English football's marquee event and the eyes of the world will be on Anfield again come Sunday.
"It just shows how remarkable that team that Jurgen Klopp built was and what they were up against," added Gibbons.
"They were obviously going against another side who it has been shown weren't playing by the same rules as everyone else."
Even in happier times, City have rarely enjoyed their trips to Anfield.
Last season's 2-1 victory was City's first win there in front of a crowd since 2003, with their other win coming amid Covid-19 restrictions in 2021.
City return to Anfield sitting top of the Premier League after a flawless start to Maresca's reign, featuring seven successive wins in all competitions.

Just months after the charges against the club were first announced in February 2023, City went on to win the treble, clinching the club's first Champions League crown, as well as the Premier League and FA Cup.
The question is whether Maresca's men can tap into that siege mentality once more, rather than wilting under the intense scrutiny.
Liverpool supporters have often created a febrile atmosphere for City's visits since they emerged as title contenders following the takeover by their Abu Dhabi-based owners in 2008.
This weekend's showdown is likely to set a new standard for vitriol directed at City's players and fans.
"It's going to be massively hostile," said Dom Farrell, author of the book "Glory Days for the Waifs and Strays" that chronicled City's rise from the third tier to European champions.
"If they were to win against Liverpool and then beat an off-form Paris Saint-Germain you really get a siege mentality going.
"But there's also a decent chance they get turned over and then it just starts to feel you're in this sort of dead zone waiting for the verdict."

ec72ef51f5f3ea8c: KUCHING: Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi heads the list of recipients of state honours, awards and medals in conjunction with the 80th birthday celebration of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar today.

5ef71553666041c2: KUALA PERLIS: It was built to move water, not tourists. Yet the Timah Tasoh flood diversion canal in Kampung Wai has gradually found a second life as one of Perlis’ more unusual places to explore.

The roughly 30-minute boat journey winds past limestone formations estimated to be 500 million years old, with thick greenery rising along the route. Its most striking section takes visitors through a 765m tunnel cutting through the Nakawan Range, where colourful lights illuminate the passage.

Tour guide Muhamad Hairi Akif Shahrun Anuar, 27, said Kampung Wai was once little known outside the area. That began to change as photographs and videos of the canal spread on social media, drawing curious visitors to see the route for themselves.
“Now many visitors are coming here because they, too, want to experience the journey,” he told Bernama.
“Some come because they are attracted by the scenery, but they become even more excited when they learn that the canal was actually built as a flood mitigation project.”

The contrast is part of its appeal. From infrastructure designed to protect lives and property, the destination now offers a close-up look at the landscape around it, combining engineering with the limestone terrain that defines much of northern Perlis.

Hairi said weekends and school holidays tend to draw the biggest crowds, including visitors from overseas. The growing interest has also created opportunities for villagers, with activities such as paddle boating, water biking and three-wheeled motorcycle rides now available around the area.

Local traders have benefited, too, selling food and drinks to visitors who stay longer in the village. For residents, the change has brought a modest tourism economy to a place that was never originally intended to become an attraction.

The canal also fits naturally into a wider trip around Perlis, where limestone landscapes are never far away. Nearby options include Gua Kelam and the Wang Kelian viewpoint, while the FRIM Mata Ayer Research Station offers another window into the state’s forest ecosystem.

Those looking for something less outdoorsy can head towards places such as Kampung Warna-Warni, Kota Kayang Museum or Padang Besar, where local and Thai influences meet in the food, shopping and everyday rhythm of the border state.
And that cross-border character extends to the table, from Perlis laksa and seafood to mango sticky rice and other delicious dishes shaped partly by neighbouring Thailand.
f83062365d4470cc: KUALA LUMPUR: Suspended Bersatu vice-president Ronald Kiandee says he is not surprised by the party's plan to sign a pact with the Pakatan Harapan-led government in Selangor.
The Beluran MP claimed the current Bersatu leadership has long sought an association with PH, adding that the move to negotiate a pact in Selangor has only made their intentions clearer.

"So now it is obvious that, all this while, they have been wanting to associate with PH,” he told FMT when met in Parliament after the tabling of the 2027 budget yesterday.
Kiandee said the pact has probably been in the works for a while now, and that former PKR leaders in Bersatu, such as Azmin Ali, Hilman Idham and Dr Afif Bahardin, could have played a role in it.

The 56-member Selangor assembly comprises 32 representatives from Pakatan Harapan, followed by Bersatu (11), PAS (10), Barisan Nasional (2), and one independent.
PAS’s image affected by Bersatu fallout

Meanwhile, PAS’s Pendang MP Awang Hashim downplayed tensions between BN and PH as well as the planned PH-Bersatu pact, saying it was natural in politics for allies to become opponents, and vice versa.
He added that Bersatu’s potential cooperation with PH in Selangor was a decision made by the party itself, despite the party still being a PN component.
“This is normal. In politics, friends can become enemies, and tomorrow, enemies may become friends. That is natural in politics.
“It would not be a surprise if Bersatu were to work with PH in Selangor. That is their right, as they have now decided not to be with PN," the two-term MP said.
Awang insisted that PAS had not anticipated the fallout within Bersatu and has actively steered clear of its coalition partner’s internal turmoil.
“Whatever happens, it will also reflect badly on the image of the coalition’s other partners.

Bersatu’s internal friction arose from an intense leadership tussle between party president Muhyiddin Yassin and then deputy Hamzah Zainudin, which saw the latter expelled in February.
Hamzah, the opposition leader, now leads Wawasan, which boasts several former Bersatu MPs and assemblymen among its ranks.
“We did not interfere, but were dragged into this situation and forced to make our own decisions,” he said.
14d9e672826edcd4: KUALA LUMPUR: Naib Presiden Bersatu yang digantung, Ronald Kiandee, berkata beliau tidak terkejut dengan rancangan partinya untuk memeterai kerjasama dengan kerajaan Selangor pimpinan Pakatan Harapan (PH).

Awang menegaskan PAS tidak menjangkakan perselisihan dalam Bersatu akan berlaku dan parti itu secara aktif mengelak daripada terheret dalam kemelut dalaman rakan gabungannya.
“Apa sahaja yang berlaku, imej rakan-rakan lain dalam gabungan itu turut akan terjejas.
“Ini masalah dalaman kamu (Bersatu), tetapi kami tidak dapat mengelak daripada menerima kesannya.”

Perselisihan dalaman Bersatu berpunca daripada perebutan kepimpinan yang sengit antara Presiden parti, Muhyiddin Yassin, dengan timbalannya ketika itu, Hamzah Zainudin, yang berakhir dengan pemecatan Hamzah pada Februari.
Hamzah, yang merupakan ketua pembangkang, kini mengetuai Wawasan, yang turut dianggotai beberapa bekas Ahli Parlimen dan Adun Bersatu.
“Kami tidak campur tangan, tetapi kami turut terheret dalam keadaan ini dan terpaksa membuat keputusan sendiri,” katanya.
5c944a78a2a47cd6: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget strikes a pragmatic balance between fiscal consolidation, economic growth and cost-of-living support, economists say.
However, its success will depend on whether public spending translates into higher household incomes, better jobs and stronger productivity.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid described the budget as pragmatic.
He said the government was seeking to maintain fiscal discipline while supporting the rakyat through targeted assistance and measures to ease financial pressures on households and businesses.
"We can see that cash transfers have been increased, alongside tax cuts for the M40 income group and small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
"Credit guarantees are also part of the budget measures to ensure SMEs continue to have access to financing," he told Business Times.

Universiti Teknologi Mara senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said the budget struck a reasonable balance between supporting economic growth, easing cost-of-living pressures and managing public finances.

He said targeted assistance and the government's commitment to reducing the fiscal deficit were among its key strengths, although the longer-term impact would depend on the effectiveness of public spending.
"The main weakness to watch is whether spending delivers sufficient productivity gains and higher-quality employment to support long-term growth.

"Ultimately, the success of the budget should be measured not only by its allocation of funds but also by whether it improves incomes, creates better jobs and strengthens the economy's capacity to withstand external shocks," he said.
DEFICIT REDUCTION MUST PRESERVE GROWTH

The federal fiscal deficit is projected to narrow to RM77.5 billion, or 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP), in 2027 from RM78.5 billion, or 3.6 per cent of GDP, in 2026, marking the sixth consecutive year of deficit reduction.

Total expenditure is projected to increase 3.6 per cent to RM459.8 billion, while development expenditure will rise 2.5 per cent to RM83 billion to support infrastructure, education, healthcare, flood mitigation and affordable housing.

Socio-Economic Research Centre executive director Lee Heng Guie said the government's continued commitment to fiscal discipline without sacrificing social and growth priorities was encouraging amid geopolitical tensions and global economic uncertainty.

He said the budget sought to provide immediate relief while advancing medium-term strategies to strengthen structural competitiveness, accelerate digital adoption and support sustainable economic growth.
However, Lee said Malaysia needed to broaden its revenue base and rationalise operating expenditure to sustain fiscal consolidation while preserving resources for productive investments.
Federal revenue is projected to grow 4.7 per cent to RM380.8 billion in 2027, while the tax-to-GDP ratio averaged 12.1 per cent in 2020-2027, compared with 13.8 per cent in 2010-2019.
Lee said the declining ratio highlighted the need to strengthen revenue collection, adding that the reintroduction of the goods and services tax was worth considering.
DEBT BURDEN CALLS FOR STRONGER REVENUE

Idham said narrowing the fiscal deficit and moderating new borrowing represented progress but would not necessarily lead to a rapid reduction in the overall debt stock as existing borrowings continued to incur interest and require servicing.
He said the government needed to sustain revenue growth, improve spending efficiency and ensure new borrowing financed productive investments capable of generating long-term economic returns.
"Equally important is maintaining a credible fiscal consolidation path without undermining essential social protection or development spending.
"The objective should be to reduce the debt burden relative to the economy while preserving sufficient fiscal space to respond to future economic shocks," Idham said.
PRODUCTIVITY AND JOBS KEY TO LONG-TERM GAINS

Idham said the government should strengthen Malaysia's competitiveness through three priorities: raising productivity and investment quality, reforming the labour market and improving public spending efficiency.

He said the government should accelerate automation, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and research and development, particularly among SMEs, to help businesses move into higher-value activities.

The labour market and skills ecosystem should also be better aligned with industry needs through technical and vocational education and training, higher education and reskilling programmes, while encouraging better wages and more high-skilled jobs.

He added that outcome-based budgeting, better coordination of government programmes and regular evaluations of incentives were needed to ensure public spending generated measurable gains in investment, employment and productivity.
"These reforms would help Malaysia compete on capabilities and innovation rather than cost alone, while supporting more sustainable and inclusive long-term growth," he said.

Meanwhile, Malaysia's economic growth is projected at between 4.2 and 5.2 per cent in 2027, compared with an estimated 4.8 to 5.3 per cent in 2026, as technology exports and investment activity moderate.
Lee cautioned that household spending remained constrained by rising living costs, food and services inflation, and elevated debt.

He said the government needed to ensure economic growth translated into broader improvements in purchasing power, as reliance on cash assistance and fuel subsidies highlighted persistent financial pressures on households.
"While overall private consumption might look stable, the underlying growth is narrow and a distinct absence of a broad-based consumption acceleration.
This indicates that consumers are not increasing their spending across retail, dining, or entertainment," he said.

0b9c331ff3215c2b: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Friday announced the appointment of conservative commentator Katie Zacharia as his new White House press secretary, praising her as a loyal supporter.
"She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning," Trump posted on his Truth Social platform.
"She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA!" he added, referring to his Make America Great Again movement.

Zacharia, a lawyer and communications adviser to Trump's media company, will succeed Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down in August after becoming one of the most prominent public faces of his second administration.
Trump praised his new spokeswoman's credentials, including her work for his presidential campaigns, and said he was confident she would enjoy a good relationship with the White House press corps.
Zacharia thanked Trump in a post on X for the "distinguished privilege of serving as White House Press Secretary".
Trump's "confidence is a true privilege, and his leadership is a blessing to this country," she wrote.
"The work ahead is to continue delivering strong results for our Country and communicating to the American people the major wins that this Administration is making every single day."
Zacharia currently serves as a senior communications adviser to Trump Media and Technology Group, which operates the president's Truth Social platform.
Trump described her work at his company as "outstanding".

A frequent commentator on conservative television networks, including Fox News and Newsmax, Zacharia previously served a brief stint as a spokeswoman for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees US immigration enforcement.
High-profile role
She joined the department under then-secretary Kristi Noem earlier this year but left after about two months, according to her LinkedIn profile.
Zacharia, who lives in California, has also worked with Fix California, a conservative advocacy group founded by Richard Grenell, a longtime Trump ally and one of his special presidential envoys.
According to CNBC, she serves as general counsel for the organisation, which seeks to advance conservative political causes in the Democratic-leaning state.
A graduate of Pepperdine University's law school, Zacharia began her career in Republican politics, working as an intern for the Republican National Committee in 2006, CNN reported.
Trump sought advice from several allies and advisers, including Leavitt, before deciding to offer Zacharia the position, according to CNN.

Her appointment fills one of the White House's most visible positions, with the press secretary responsible for briefing journalists, fielding questions about administration policies and serving as a chief public defender of the president.
Leavitt, who took up the position when Trump returned to power in January 2025, became the youngest White House press secretary in US history at 27.
A staunch Trump loyalist who previously served as press secretary for his 2024 presidential campaign, she left the administration in late August following the birth of her second child.
Fox News announced this week that Leavitt would join the conservative network as an on-air contributor beginning in November.
Trump praised his outgoing spokeswoman, saying she had done a "fantastic job" in the role.
