e2f2d784cd7852cf: BRASILIA: Brazilian prosecutors on Friday filed an unprecedented lawsuit against oil giant Shell's subsidiary in the country, demanding US$108 million in compensation over deadly 2024 floods.
Torrential rains sparked historic flooding in southern Brazil in April and May of that year, leaving nearly 200 people dead, 500,000 more displaced and massive damages.
According to the lawsuit, Shell's liability should match its contribution to global warming -- estimated at two percent of historical global greenhouse gas emissions.

"This civil suit is aimed at holding the defendant company accountable, in terms of its environmental and climate-related responsibilities, for collective material and moral damages stemming from the extreme weather event that hit Rio Grande do Sul state," public prosecutors said, according to court documents seen by AFP.
They said the British energy giant should be held responsible because of its past and current greenhouse gas emissions associated with exploration, production and sale of fossil fuels.
The US$108 million in compensation accounts for both material and moral damages.

The filing of a new climate-related suit by Brazilian prosecutors -- in conjunction with Instituto Preservar, a Brazilian NGO -- marks a new phase in the global battle in the courts against oil giants.

"This is the first time a national public prosecutor is suing an oil major for a climate disaster," Maria Antonia Tigre, the director of global climate litigation at the Sabin Center for Climate Change Law, told AFP.
Shell is already being sued in the United Kingdom by victims of a typhoon in the Philippines.
3a298d6377b0d359: PETALING JAYA: The government's offer of more permanent positions for contract doctors must be complemented with measures to improve their retention in the public health system, says a public health researcher.

Ilyana Mukhriz, a research associate at the Khazanah Research Institute, said permanent appointments alone would not resolve the challenges of retaining doctors even though they were a significant step towards improving job security.

"One budget allocation cannot fix it all, but the next steps should be to ensure that doctors have decent working conditions, clear communication of career progression potential, more adequate permanent senior posts using cluster- and merit-based warrants as well as fair remuneration," she told FMT.
She said doctors posted to rural areas should also have adequate living quarters, rest facilities and access to basic necessities.

The government announced in the 2027 budget estimates tabled on Friday that more than 9,000 contract doctors would be offered permanent positions next year. Doctors who successfully complete their housemanship would also be offered permanent appointments as medical officers.

But Ilyana pointed out that some doctors had previously failed to report for duty despite receiving permanent offers. Last week, health minister Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said only 63% of medical officers offered permanent postings in Sabah and Sarawak this year had reported for duty.
On a separate matter, Ilyana said the 2027 budget should have placed greater emphasis on preventing chronic diseases through education and programmes encouraging behavioural changes.
"If we do not tackle the rise in chronic diseases, we will end up spending more in future to provide curative care," she said.
She also called for better procurement and maintenance of medical equipment because "some hospital assets were beyond repair".

The Galen Centre health policy think tank said converting existing contract doctor posts into permanent positions would not necessarily increase the number of healthcare professionals delivering services.

Its CEO, Azrul Khalib, called for a funded, multi-year recruitment and retention programme and the establishment of an independent health services commission to improve recruitment, deployment, remuneration and career progression.
He said the 2027 budget had missed an opportunity to undertake structural healthcare reforms, as increased spending alone would not solve the problems affecting the system.
“The budget provides relief in several important areas. However, it avoids the difficult decisions necessary to make healthcare sustainable, affordable and accessible over the next decade,” he said.
The budget estimates contain an allocation of RM47 billion for the health ministry, a slight increase from the RM46 billion for 2026.

Other measures include more than RM770 million for modern medical equipment, RM200 million to outsource patient treatment to other hospitals to reduce waiting times, RM1.2 billion for maintenance of public healthcare facilities, the introduction of the MediAsas medical insurance scheme, and the nationwide rollout of electronic medical records.
32c8d0b9a2ded0c8: THE haunting and heartbreaking remake of Stephen King's legendary horror story 'Carrie' has arrived. Directed by acclaimed filmmaker Mike Flanagan ('The Haunting of Hill House'), the eight-episode series premiered globally on Prime Video on Oct 7.
Adapted for television for the very first time, this fresh take expands King's 1974 debut novel into a deeply personal, modern tragedy.
The story follows Carrie White (Summer H. Howell), a misfit teenager raised in isolation by her fiercely protective, devout mother Margaret White (Samantha Sloyan).

When her father's sudden death forces Carrie into the brutal world of public high school, she is thrust into a viral bullying scandal, the relentless pressure of the social media age and the dangerous awakening of her own telekinetic powers.
A FRESH FACE IN A LEGENDARY ROLE
Landing the iconic role of Carrie was no small feat for newcomer Howell, who was chosen after a search involving nearly 1,500 actors.
Interestingly, Howell went into the audition without prior knowledge of the story.
"I hadn't seen any of the films or read the book," Howell told the 'New Straits Times' in a recent online interview.

"After getting the role, I asked Mike if he wanted me to read it. He said 'no' — we agreed it was best for me to focus on creating my own version of Carrie. We actually ended up watching the 1976 film together with the cast after we wrapped shooting!"
For Howell, capturing Carrie's journey meant tapping into universal teenage anxieties.
"Carrie is experiencing the world and people for the first time. I went to public school, so I remembered how uncomfortable those years could feel," she explained.
"Showing Carrie's initial curiosity and gratitude for the outside world was so important to me. At her core, she's optimistic, genuinely kind and just trying to fit in."
Of course, playing Carrie also meant tackling horror's most famous sequence: the shower scene.
"We spent a full day filming it," Howell recalled.

"It was exhausting with all the stunts and intense emotion, but the cast made it fun. At one point, I was sitting on a box off-camera while the other girls threw pads and tampons at the lens for a POV shot. It was crazy, but I love how it turned out."
MOTHER, MONSTER OR PROTECTOR?

Sloyan — a familiar face in Flanagan's projects — was initially worried the role might mirror her fanatically religious character, Beverly Keane, from 'Midnight Mass'. However, Flanagan had an entirely different vision for Margaret.

"He was imagining a brand-new Margaret — anchored first and foremost in love for her daughter. The tragedy comes from fear. Her ferocity and what makes her dangerous is her desperate reaction to that fear; the lengths she'll go to protect Carrie."
Sloyan highlights the striking contrast between mother and daughter as they step out into society together.

"Neither of them has left their home in 15 years. But while Carrie meets the world with curiosity and hope, Margaret meets it with suspicion and fear. If she feels Carrie is threatened, she puts on armour and goes to war."
Despite the intense on-screen dynamic, the bond off-camera was immediate.
"Filming with Sam (Sloyan) felt like a dream," Howell shared.
"Even when our characters were at odds, we made sure the love between them was always visible."
TIMELY THEMES FOR A MODERN WORLD
While Brian De Palma's Oscar-nominated 1976 feature film cemented 'Carrie' in pop culture history, Flanagan felt the story needed a modern reckoning.
"My oldest son was about to start secondary school, and as I wrestled with normal parental anxiety, I marvelled at how relevant King's core themes still are.
"Cruelty, empathy, bullying and school violence are even more crucial conversations today than they were 50 years ago."
Flanagan noted that the Internet and social media have reshaped youth culture in ways King couldn't have predicted in the 1970s.
Through its eight-episode runtime, the series explores how small, everyday choices can cascade into tragedy.
Ultimately, the cast hopes the series leaves viewers with a simple message.
"If you take anything away from watching 'Carrie', I hope it's to be kind," Howell concluded.
"It's so easy to be mean just to fit in, especially when hiding behind a screen. It takes real bravery to be kind."
'Carrie' is written and produced by Flanagan, with King also serving as executive producer.
Other cast members are Matthew Lillard, Heather Graham, Amber Midthunder, Rahul Kohli, Kate Siegel, Josie Totah and Arthur Conti.

0a482e5bd1d730b2: Inisiatif berfasa kerajaan untuk membubarkan sistem kontrak bagi pegawai perubatan menjelang 2028 di bawah reformasi perkhidmatan awam merupakan satu langkah maju yang amat dipuji. Pasukan Petugas Bersama Antara Kementerian (IMJTF) Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM) menyasarkan, menjelang 2028, setiap pegawai perubatan siswazah (doktor pelatih) yang menamatkan latihan akan ditawarkan jawatan tetap secara serta-merta. Bersama rancangan untuk menyerap baki doktor kontrak secara berperingkat sepanjang 2027, pencapaian penting ini bakal meleraikan kemelut sistemik yang berlarutan sekian lama.

Pelbagai langkah juga diperkenalkan bagi menggalakkan lebih ramai pegawai perubatan muda berkhidmat di Sabah dan Sarawak. Inisiatif ini termasuk menambah baik sistem penempatan, menanggung sepenuhnya kos perpindahan, serta memberikan mata merit tambahan bagi latihan pakar dan permohonan cuti belajar kepada mereka yang ditempatkan di kedua-dua wilayah tersebut.

Bagaimanapun, jika kementerian benar-benar mahu membasmi ketidaktentuan kerjaya doktor muda, ia mesti mengekalkan momentum ini melalui ketelusan dasar yang mutlak. Jaminan jawatan tetap tidak membawa makna yang besar jika struktur pekerjaan itu sendiri kekal tidak mampan.

Laluan untuk mendapatkan jawatan tetap bukan lagi alat pengekalan bakat mutlak seperti dahulu. KKM kini berdepan dengan penyusutan bakat yang berterusan, apabila pegawai perubatan tetap terus meletak jawatan akibat tekanan beban kerja yang runcing.

Punca utama kepada rantaian tindakan ini ialah persekitaran operasi. Beban kerja yang melampau dan kelesuan upaya (burnout) yang teruk—diburukkan lagi oleh waktu tugasan atas panggilan (on-call) yang panjang serta kekurangan kakitangan yang kritikal di fasiliti utama—secara langsung menjejaskan kesejahteraan mental dan fizikal pegawai barisan hadapan. Budaya tempat kerja yang toksik, terutamanya isu buli yang berterusan, terus menggugat kesihatan emosi mereka.

Tekanan struktur ini diperhebat lagi oleh kepincangan dalam sistem e-Penempatan. Pertukaran wilayah secara mendadak tanpa persediaan rapi, ditambah pula dengan ketidaksetaraan dalam elaun perpindahan sebelum ini, sering kali menyebabkan doktor berasa terperangkap, sekali gus melihat peletakan jawatan sebagai satu-satunya jalan keluar yang munasabah. Apabila digabungkan dengan pengorbanan peribadi—sama ada menguruskan logistik keluarga, mengendali cabaran kesihatan kronik, atau membiayai laluan kepakaran secara kendiri—sistem kesihatan awam menjadi semakin sukar untuk dipertahankan oleh bakat muda.
Pelan jalar strategik untuk pengekalan sistemik
Bagi memelihara integriti perkhidmatan kesihatan negara, kerajaan mesti mengimbangi ikrar pengambilan pekerja dengan intervensi struktur yang mendalam:

Restrukturisasi ganjaran kewangan: Kerajaan mesti merapatkan jurang pendapatan antara sektor awam dan swasta melalui semakan berkala ke atas gaji dan elaun. Langkah ini termasuk menilai semula elaun perkhidmatan kritikal, menaikkan kadar elaun on-call, dan memperkenalkan model insentif khusus untuk pakar klinikal kanan. Selain itu, pelanjutan kadar bayaran locum yang adil adalah penting bagi memastikan setiap jam kerja lebih masa dibayar dengan pampasan kewangan yang setimpal.

Reformasi budaya tempat kerja: KKM mesti beralih daripada sekadar retorik kepada penguatkuasaan ketat berhubung dasar sifar toleransi terhadap gejala buli di hospital. Pengenalan jadual kerja yang lebih manusiawi dan fleksibel merupakan prasyarat utama untuk mengurangkan kelesuan upaya yang kronik.

Logistik e-Penempatan yang telus: Mekanisme e-Penempatan mesti beroperasi dengan jangkaan yang jelas, memberikan tempoh notis yang munasabah kepada doktor untuk menguruskan kehidupan peribadi mereka. Penerapan pilihan penempatan sukarela atau keutamaan wilayah akan melonjakkan moral mereka secara ketara. Paling utama, elaun perpindahan penuh mesti diagihkan secara saksama merentas semua tempoh perkhidmatan bagi membendung kejutan kewangan akibat pertukaran antara negeri.

Jaminan laluan kepakaran: Akses kepada program pascasiswazah lanjutan, sama ada melalui Hadiah Latihan Persekutuan (HLP) atau laluan selari (parallel pathway), mesti diperluas dan dipermudah. Doktor muda perlu melihat trajektori jangka panjang yang jelas dan ganjaran yang berbaloi dalam perkhidmatan awam.

Mengekalkan tenaga kerja perubatan awam kita adalah jauh lebih penting daripada sekadar menjaga kebajikan asas pekerja; ia merupakan pelaburan kritikal dalam kedaulatan dan daya tahan kerangka kesihatan Malaysia. Trend peletakan jawatan memaparkan realiti yang jelas: persekitaran yang toksik dan ketidakstabilan kerjaya adalah pemacu utama kepada penghijrahan bakat kita.

Dengan mengimbangi ikrar pelantikan tetap 2028 bersama kemas kini kewangan dan tempat kerja yang bermakna lagi sistemik, KKM mampu mengubah keadaan ini. Memelihara tenaga kerja kesihatan yang kompeten dan bermotivasi tinggi adalah satu-satunya jalan mutlak untuk memastikan setiap rakyat Malaysia terus mendapat akses kepada penjagaan yang saksama, berkualiti tinggi, dan mampu ditanggung.

5724ecb12ef259ab: From Moaz Nair
The government’s phased initiative to dismantle the contract system for medical officers by 2028 under civil service reforms is a commendable stride forward.

The health ministry's Inter-Ministerial Joint Task Force (IMJTF) targets that, by 2028, every single graduate medical officer (houseman) who completes training will be offered a permanent role immediately.
Alongside plans to absorb remaining contract doctors in waves throughout 2027, this milestone stands to dissolve years of systemic gridlock.

Various measures have also been introduced to encourage more young medical officers to serve in Sabah and Sarawak. These initiatives include improving the placement system, fully covering relocation expenses, and granting additional merit points for specialist training and study leave applications to those deployed in the two regions.

However, if the ministry truly wants to eradicate career uncertainty for young doctors, it must maintain momentum through absolute policy transparency. Permanent job security means little if the job itself remains structurally unsustainable.
The underlying crisis

Securing a permanent position is no longer the ultimate retention tool it once was. The ministry faces an ongoing talent drain, as permanent medical officers continue to resign due to acute workforce pressures.

Chief among these triggers is the operational environment. Extreme workloads and severe burnout—compounded by gruelling on-call hours and systemic understaffing at key facilities—are directly eroding the mental and physical well-being of frontline officers. A toxic workplace culture, notably the persistence of bullying, further compromises their emotional health.

This structural stress is intensified by friction within the e-Placement system. Abrupt, ill-prepared regional transfers, combined with historical inequities in relocation allowances, have frequently left physicians feeling trapped, viewing resignation as the only reasonable exit strategy.

When coupled with personal sacrifices—whether managing family logistics, navigating chronic health challenges, or funding independent specialist pathways—the public healthcare system becomes increasingly difficult to justify for young talent.
Strategic roadmap for systemic retention
To preserve the integrity of our national health service, the state must match its hiring pledges with deep, structural interventions:

Restructuring financial rewards: the government must bridge the income gap between the public and private sectors through periodic reviews of salaries and allowances. This measure includes reassessing the critical service allowance, increasing on-call allowance rates, and introducing specialised incentive models for senior clinical specialists. Furthermore, extending fair locum payment rates is essential to ensure that every hour of overtime is met with commensurate financial compensation.

Reforming workplace culture: the ministry must shift from rhetoric to strict enforcement regarding its zero-tolerance policy against hospital bullying. Introducing humane, flexible scheduling is a prerequisite to mitigating chronic burnout.

Transparent e-Placement logistics: the e-Placement mechanism must operate with predictability, affording doctors reasonable notice windows to arrange their personal lives. Incorporating voluntary placement options or regional preferences would heavily boost morale. Crucially, full relocation allowances must be distributed equitably across all tenures to curb the financial shocks of interstate transfers.

Securing specialisation pathways: access to advanced postgraduate tracks, whether via the federal training award (HLP) or parallel pathways, must be expanded and streamlined. Young physicians need to see an unambiguous, rewarding long-term trajectory within the public civil service.
The bottom line

Retaining our public medical workforce goes far beyond baseline worker welfare; it is a critical investment in the sovereignty and resilience of Malaysia’s healthcare framework. The resignation trends tell a clear story: toxic environments and career instability are the primary drivers of our talent flight.

By balancing the 2028 permanent employment pledge with meaningful, systemic workplace and financial updates, the ministry can successfully turn the tide. Safeguarding a competent and motivated healthcare workforce is the only definitive way to ensure every Malaysian retains access to equitable, high-quality and affordable care.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.

7c010cc1645d290c: PETALING JAYA: It is tempting to think that, in 2026, scientists have already catalogued most of the creatures sharing the planet with us. Yet in the forests of Borneo, an insect small enough to disappear into leaf litter may still turn out to be something science has never formally recorded.

That possibility emerged during a recent 10-day expedition to Tangkulap Forest Reserve in Sabah, where an international team of entomologists went searching for crickets, grasshoppers, mantises, dragonflies and other insects.

According to a report by Le Monde, one of the more intriguing finds was a small, apparently mute cricket belonging to the genus Paranisitra. The insect may prove to be a new species - and, notably, the genus itself had not previously been recorded in Borneo.

For the scientists involved, that is the kind of moment that keeps fieldwork irresistible. French cricket specialist Tony Robillard, who led the expedition, was quoted as saying: “I think I’ve found something incredible.”
Tangkulap Forest Reserve covers more than 27,000ha in Sabah, providing the sort of dense tropical habitat where an extraordinary amount of life can remain hidden in plain sight.

Much of the expedition took place after dark, when headlamps replaced daylight and scientists combed through vegetation, tree roots and leaf litter for specimens. The work may sound rather less glamorous than spotting an orangutan or pygmy elephant, but insects make up an enormous part of tropical biodiversity.

They are also essential to how forests function. Insects pollinate plants, break down dead material, recycle nutrients and provide food for countless other animals; some are also useful indicators of the overall health of an ecosystem, a role highlighted by the Sabah forestry department during a tropical-insect workshop earlier this year.
Yet scientists believe only a fraction of the world’s insect species have been formally identified.
That leaves forests such as those in Sabah with an intriguing possibility: creatures that have been flying, crawling and chirping there for generations may still have no scientific name.
Finding one is only the beginning

Discovering an unusual insect in the forest does not immediately make it a new species. Researchers must compare specimens with known species, examine physical features and, increasingly, study their DNA before determining whether they have genuinely found something previously undescribed.
There is another complication. Some “new” insects may already be sitting unnoticed in museum collections, collected decades ago but never studied closely enough to be formally identified.

That makes modern taxonomy a curious mixture of adventure and painstaking detective work: part night-time jungle expedition, part laboratory analysis, and sometimes part rummage through drawers of specimens gathered long before the researchers were born.
It might be tempting to wonder why identifying one more cricket matters in a forest already teeming with insects. The answer is that it is difficult to protect a species if nobody knows it exists.
Knowing what lives in a forest helps scientists understand how ecosystems fit together, which species are rare or restricted to particular habitats, and what may disappear when those habitats change.

That work is especially significant in a biodiversity-rich region such as Sabah, where forests continue to face pressure from land-use change and other human activity. Sabah still retains millions of hectares of forest reserve, with areas managed for conservation, research, wildlife protection and sustainable forestry.
The possible Paranisitra discovery has yet to be formally confirmed as a new species. But perhaps that uncertainty is part of its charm.

In one of the world’s most studied eras, Borneo can still offer scientists the thrill of lifting a leaf and finding something that makes them stop, look twice - and wonder whether anyone has ever described it before.
47b76331684e19c8: KATHMANDU: Nepal's president on Friday shortened the waiting period to declare missing disaster victims dead from 12 years to about 1.5 months, as thousands remain unaccounted for following the Himalayan country's devastating flood.
The catastrophic flood on Aug 26 was triggered by a mountain and glacier collapse on the China-Nepal border.
The tsunami-like floodwaters swept through several districts, destroying roads, bridges and hydropower dams and killing more than 1,400 people.
More than 5,000 people remain missing, including hundreds of foreign nationals.
Under prior Nepalese law, a person had to be missing for 12 years before they could be legally declared dead.

"The 12-year period is being reduced to around 45 days," government spokesman Sasmit Pokharel told reporters this week after a cabinet meeting forwarded an ordinance updating the timeline to the president.
Kiran Pokharel, press advisor to president Ram Chandra Poudel told AFP on Friday that the "ordinance relating to disaster laws has been issued", without sharing details of the amendments.
So far, just 112 bodies have been identified and returned to their families.
Rescue teams spent weeks searching through metres of mud and sediment and combing through flood-damaged homes for survivors and victims.
More than a month after the disaster, families of missing victims have been unable to obtain death certificates, preventing them from accessing compensations or resolving property issues.
Some families have already held symbolic cremation ceremonies for relatives who remain missing.
4af311b3c593a7d0: NEW YORK: Protesters gathered in New York on Friday after Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers shot a Dominican man in an incident that has provoked a showdown between the city's Democratic mayor and the Trump administration.
Oscar Bergal, 28, was wounded in the neck during an ICE operation in the Bronx on Thursday, while a five-year-old child who was in his car at the time was physically unharmed.

The shooting drew swift criticism from Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who wrote "Abolish ICE" on X — a common refrain among the political left opposed to Republican President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown.
US Homeland Security chief Markwayne Mullin lashed out in response, telling reporters that Mamdani's words were "dangerous and incite hostility".
"Mayor, if you abolish ICE, who's going to take criminals off the streets of your own town?" Mullin said. "Who's going to take the murderers and the thieves and the gangbangers?"
An AFP journalist saw hundreds of protesters stretching across several blocks in Manhattan on Friday, chanting "No hate, no fear, immigrants are welcome here" and "No ICE".
New York, a Democratic stronghold, is one of several US cities that bar their police forces from assisting with federal immigration enforcement.
Mamdani said on Thursday that he was seeking to speak with Trump and would demand that immigration agents be withdrawn from the city.
The incident could test the surprisingly warm relationship between the two leaders.
Video of the shooting, shared by US media on Friday, shows what appears to be a plainclothes federal agent rushing towards a silver car with a gun drawn.
The vehicle briefly reverses as the agent punches the driver-side window, before a second plainclothes officer draws a gun.
He points the weapon at the driver as the car pulls away off screen, appearing to collide with the side of a passing vehicle.
High-profile shootings
Mullin said Bergal had an extensive criminal history and was trying to evade arrest.
"He came to this country legally a few years ago, and ever since he's come in, he's committed crime and crime after crime," the Homeland Security secretary said.
Mullin said ICE officers did not know there was a child in the car when they opened fire.
Marcos Charles, a senior ICE official, told reporters that Bergal had "refused lawful orders to exit his vehicle".
"He then accelerated his vehicle, smashing into two of our government ICE vehicles, and then weaponised his vehicle and proceeded to accelerate, going towards other officers," Charles said.
"Our officers, using their training, and believing that their life and the lives of their partners and general public were in danger, used their training and fired weapons," he said.
ICE agents, who often wear civilian clothing and cover their faces, have been involved in several high-profile shootings this year.
Ruben Ray Martinez, 23, was shot by ICE in March 2025 in what the Texas Tribune said was the first known killing of an American by immigration agents during Trump's second term.
More recently, a Mexican man, Lorenzo Salgado, died in July after being shot by an ICE officer in Houston, Texas.

Two Americans — Renee Good and Alex Pretti — were shot and killed by federal immigration agents in separate incidents in Minnesota during a crackdown on undocumented migrants in the northern state earlier this year.

750652d6015a7caf: BRASILIA: Brazilian prosecutors on Friday filed an unprecedented lawsuit against oil giant Shell's subsidiary in the country, demanding US$108 million in compensation over deadly 2024 floods.
Torrential rains sparked historic flooding in southern Brazil in April and May of that year, leaving nearly 200 people dead, 500,000 more displaced and causing massive damage.
According to the lawsuit, Shell's liability should match its contribution to global warming, estimated at two per cent of historical global greenhouse gas emissions.

"This civil suit is aimed at holding the defendant company accountable, in terms of its environmental and climate-related responsibilities, for collective material and moral damages stemming from the extreme weather event that hit Rio Grande do Sul state," public prosecutors said, according to court documents seen by AFP.
They said the British energy giant should be held responsible because of its past and current greenhouse gas emissions associated with the exploration, production and sale of fossil fuels.
The US$108 million in compensation covers both material and moral damages.
The filing of a new climate-related lawsuit by Brazilian prosecutors, in conjunction with Instituto Preservar, a Brazilian NGO, marks a new phase in the global legal battle against oil giants.

"This is the first time a national public prosecutor is suing an oil major for a climate disaster," Maria Antonia Tigre, director of global climate litigation at the Sabin Center for Climate Change Law, told AFP.
Shell is already being sued in the United Kingdom by victims of a typhoon in the Philippines.
c9d5b583d8b4fcb8: NEW YORK: President Donald Trump asked the US Supreme Court on Friday to revive his dismissed lawsuit against his 2016 Democratic rival Hillary Clinton, accusing her, former FBI Director James Comey and others of conspiring to rig that year's election by linking his campaign to Russia.

The Republican president filed his appeal after a federal judge threw out the case and imposed nearly US$1 million in sanctions against Trump and one of his lawyers for bringing a "frivolous" suit. A US appeals court subsequently upheld the dismissal and sanctions.

In 2022, after losing the 2020 election and leaving office, Trump sued Clinton, Comey, former British intelligence officer Christopher Steele, the Democratic National Committee and numerous others in a lengthy complaint filed in federal court in Florida.

Trump, who has a history of suing adversaries, alleged that in the lead-up to the 2016 election, Clinton conspired with allies to discredit him with a "false narrative" that he and his campaign colluded with Russia.
The lengthy suit alleged "racketeering" and a "conspiracy to commit injurious falsehood", among other claims.
Trump defeated Clinton in that election, despite losing the national popular vote, and served his first term in office from 2017 to 2021.

US government officials have accused Russia of meddling in the 2016 election, and an investigation led by former FBI chief Robert Mueller documented extensive contacts between the Trump campaign and Russian operatives who sought to influence the election in his favour. Trump has called the idea of Russian interference a "hoax".

Since losing to Democrat Joe Biden in 2020, Trump has made false claims of widespread voting fraud in that year's election. Trump regained the presidency by defeating Democrat Kamala Harris in 2024 and has continued to make those false claims.
'Political manifesto'

US District Judge Donald Middlebrooks dismissed Trump's lawsuit against Clinton, citing numerous inadequacies, including that Trump had waited too long to bring some of the claims. The judge likened Trump's lawsuit to a "two-hundred-page political manifesto outlining his grievances against those that have opposed him".

Middlebrooks later ordered Trump and his lead attorney in the case, Alina Habba, to pay nearly US$1 million in fees and costs, imposing the sanctions for bringing a case that the judge said was intended "to dishonestly advance a political narrative". The judge also faulted Trump and his lawyers for a "continuing pattern of misuse of the courts".
Middlebrooks found that the lawsuit used abusive litigation tactics, contained "knowingly false" factual allegations and asserted "frivolous" legal theories.
The Atlanta-based 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the judge's rulings in 2025, including the sanctions.
"Many of Trump's and Habba's legal arguments were indeed frivolous," the 11th Circuit stated.
In court papers, lawyers for Trump and Habba said the lower courts' decisions were having a "profound impact on the presidency, and the nation as a whole".
Mueller, serving as a special counsel appointed by the Justice Department, issued a 2019 report on his investigation.

The report stated that Russia "interfered in the 2016 presidential election in sweeping and systematic fashion", but also stated that "the investigation did not establish that members of the Trump campaign conspired or coordinated with the Russian government in its election interference activities".
Mueller said in his report that he found "numerous links" and that the Trump campaign "expected it would benefit" from Russia's effort to tilt the ballot in Trump's favour.
Trump's then-Attorney General William Barr appointed a different special counsel, John Durham, in 2019 to investigate potential missteps by the FBI.

In a 2023 report, Durham concluded that the FBI lacked "actual evidence" to investigate Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and relied too heavily on tips provided by Trump's political opponents to fuel the probe.

Trump's Justice Department last year indicted Comey, one of several adversaries of the president to face criminal charges, accusing him of making false statements and obstructing Congress after he was accused of lying about authorising leaks to the news media.
A federal judge subsequently dismissed the indictment, finding that the prosecutor Trump had handpicked to prosecute Comey was unlawfully appointed.

Steele, working for an opposition research firm hired by a law firm on behalf of the Clinton campaign and the Democratic National Committee, produced a dossier alleging ties between Trump's campaign and Russia, as well as other salacious accusations, all of which Trump denied.

1f42c3e89074eed4: WASHINGTON: Condemnation of US plans for a public execution by military firing squad escalated on Friday, as Vice President JD Vance cast doubt on whether it would be livestreamed as proposed and insisted he would not watch if it was.
Nidal Hasan's execution — scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by US military firing squad since 1945.
Asked about the planned livestream, Vance told journalists he did not "know that that's actually going to happen".

"This is a guy who committed, in my view, the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside of 9/11," Vance said, but added that if the execution was broadcast live, "I'm not going to be watching it".
Representative Austin Scott of President Donald Trump's Republican Party said he supported executing Hasan but that "livestreaming executions is what jihadists do. America is better than that".

Senator Mark Kelly, a Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, said Hasan should "face justice" but that public executions were "the kind of thing Iran and the Taliban do. Is this who we want to be associated with?"
A Pentagon official told AFP on Thursday that the execution would be streamed live, after US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said "we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public".
But Trump on Friday contradicted Hegseth's confirmation and said no decision had yet been made on whether to publicly broadcast the execution, which he supports.
"They are making a determination about that, but he will be killed," Trump said. "I really don't care how he goes, as long as he goes."
Tech firms YouTube, Meta and X did not immediately respond to requests for comment on whether they would allow the execution to be streamed on their platforms.
TikTok directed AFP to its policy banning depictions of "graphic incidents and violence", including "the shooting of an individual".

The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights condemned the move, saying in a message sent to AFP on Friday that "the livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture".
Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, said it was a "barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered".
'Compound the cruelty'
Hegseth said it would be the military's first firing squad execution since World War II.
"People need to understand that...there's serious consequence for these types of things," Hegseth said in a video shared on Thursday on official Pentagon X accounts.
The last US military execution was carried out in 1961, when John Bennett was hanged for rape and attempted murder.
The Death Penalty Information Center says 135 troops have been executed by the US military since 1916.
According to rights group Amnesty International, at least 17 public executions are known to have been carried out in 2025 — six in Afghanistan and 11 in Iran.
Amnesty's Justin Mazzola said on Friday that the death penalty was "a violation of human rights" and that streaming Hasan's execution "would only compound the cruelty".
Twelve of the 13 people Hasan killed and 30 of those he wounded were soldiers. He was shot by a civilian police officer who responded to the attack and is paralysed from the waist down.
Hasan chose to conduct his own defence during the trial but called no witnesses, gave no testimony and made no attempt to deny the charges.
He was sentenced to death by a military jury in 2013.
Court-appointed defence attorneys expressed concern that he was seeking execution.

The court that convicted Hasan was told he opposed the US military's occupations of Iraq and Afghanistan and had spoken online with an alleged Al-Qaeda figure, radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki, an American citizen who was subsequently killed in a US drone strike in Yemen.

a8d5a5f59598384d: KUALA LUMPUR: A swollen gland, lingering fever or unusual tiredness in a child will usually have a common explanation. But when symptoms do not go away, parents may understandably begin to wonder whether something more serious is happening.
Lymphoma, a cancer of the lymphatic system, can affect both adults and children, although the types seen in younger patients often behave differently and require different approaches to treatment.

Consultant physician and haematologist Dr Haris Fadzillah Abdul Rahman said children are more likely to develop fast-growing forms of lymphoma, including lymphoblastic lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma and anaplastic large-cell lymphoma.
Hodgkin lymphoma is also seen in younger patients, particularly adolescents and young adults.
Adults, by contrast, can develop a wider range of lymphomas, including slower-growing forms that are relatively uncommon in children.

These differences matter because lymphoma is not a single disease: its biology, genetic changes and behaviour can vary considerably, which is why doctors first need to establish the precise subtype before deciding on treatment.
Personalised treatment
While chemotherapy remains an important part of treatment for many childhood lymphomas, particularly because some fast-growing forms respond very well to it, it is no longer the only option.
Advances in understanding how lymphoma cells grow and survive have led to treatments that target particular features of the cancer or help the immune system recognise and attack it.
Consultant paediatrician and paediatric haematologist and oncologist Dr Kogilavani Gunasagaran said the goal in treating children extends well beyond getting them into remission.

“Children have a much longer life expectancy after treatment. Therefore, doctors need to consider not only curing the lymphoma today, but also the patient’s health 10, 20 or 50 years later,” she said.
“The goal is increasingly to achieve a cure while minimising the long-term impact of treatment. In paediatric oncology, survival alone is no longer enough."
Treatment options, as such, may include targeted therapy, immunotherapy, stem-cell or bone-marrow transplantation, and an emerging approach known as CAR-T cell therapy.
“Newer treatments do not simply replace chemotherapy,” Haris pointed out. “Rather, we now have a much larger treatment toolbox.”
Depending on the child and lymphoma subtype, treatment may involve a combination of approaches.
Targeted treatment, for example, aims to attack specific features of lymphoma cells rather than broadly affecting all rapidly dividing cells.
Immunotherapy, meanwhile, works differently by helping the body’s own immune system recognise and fight lymphoma cells.
In the longer term, combinations of targeted therapy and immunotherapy may allow chemotherapy to be reduced or even avoided in selected patients.
Chances of recovery

For many children diagnosed with lymphoma, the outlook can be encouraging, although it varies according to the subtype, stage, molecular characteristics, response to treatment and whether the cancer returns.
Kogilavani said childhood Hodgkin lymphoma has one of the highest cure rates in paediatric oncology, with around 90-95% of children and adolescents able to be cured.
For childhood and adolescent non-Hodgkin lymphoma, five-year relative survival was about 90% between 2013 and 2019, although outcomes vary between subtypes and risk groups.
These improvements have come not only from new medicines but also from better disease classification, more tailored treatment, and advances in supportive care.
In the future, genomic and molecular testing, targeted therapies, immunotherapy and cellular treatments may make care even more personalised.
For children in particular, the aim is no longer simply to survive lymphoma: increasingly, treatment is about helping them reach adulthood with as few long-term effects as possible.
ae2c37cb109f02a4: PETALING JAYA: Anti-graft watchdogs have urged Putrajaya to stop allowing private intermediaries to hold public funds when facilitating government collections, following the revelation that Zetrix AI Bhd owes RM314 million in arrears.
Transparency International Malaysia (TI-M) said future concession agreements for fee collections must include strict contractual safeguards to prevent major revenue defaults.
TI-M president Raymon Ram suggested that revenue collections be paid directly into the government's accounts, with vendors paid separately by the relevant agency.

"The starting principle should be simple. A private service provider may facilitate the collection of government revenue, but it should never accumulate or exercise discretionary control over large amounts of public money," he told FMT.

"Contracts should contain predetermined suspension triggers so that a vendor cannot continue accumulating public revenue while repeated notices are being issued,” Raymon said, adding that future concession contracts should have strict enforcement mechanisms.

Transport minister Loke Siew Fook revealed earlier this week that MYEG subsidiary Zetrix AI Bhd had racked up RM314 million in unremitted road tax fees and traffic summonses collected on behalf of the road transport department (JPJ) since May.

JPJ suspended the company’s collection services on Oct 5. It was also reported that JPJ had issued 35 notices and held four engagement sessions, which ultimately prompted Zetrix AI to submit a settlement proposal to Putrajaya.

According to Loke, the company, formerly known as MyEG Services Bhd, then submitted a cheque worth RM231 million. However, the bank later advised that it was instructed by Zetrix not to process the payment.
Raymon criticised the five-month delay in taking decisive action against Zetrix, arguing that merely issuing repeated notices while arrears continued to mount was an ineffective control mechanism.
"Thirty-five reminders cannot be regarded as an adequate control mechanism when hundreds of millions of ringgit in public revenue are involved," he said.
Raymon urged Putrajaya to launch an independent forensic audit to establish a clear chronology of events dating back to the first missed remittance.
"Accountability must also follow the decision-making chain and should not stop at junior officers, if senior officials knew of the accumulating exposure and had the authority to intervene," he said.
Center to Combat Corruption and Cronyism (C4) senior research officer Bryan Cheah cautioned against placing immediate blame on ministry personnel, citing the repeated notices and bounced cheque.
Cheah, however, said the authorities should probe if there were elements of corruption behind the unremitted funds.

"C4 invites the government to reassess current procurement policies to ensure contracts and concessions given to private sector players adhere to a strict code of conduct that would include a set protocol for actions to be taken should non-compliance with contract terms occur,” he said.
The core objective of sound public administration is preventive oversight, he added, pointing out that punitive measures only act after the fact.

"By nature, penalties are responses in situations where a breach or violation of terms has occurred. The purpose of good governance is to ensure such occurrences do not take place to begin with," Cheah said.
65700b688f7301c3: PETALING JAYA: Badan pemantau antirasuah menggesa Putrajaya supaya menghentikan amalan membenarkan orang tengah swasta memegang wang awam ketika mengurus kutipan kerajaan, susulan pendedahan bahawa Zetrix AI Bhd mempunyai tunggakan sebanyak RM314 juta.

Transparency International Malaysia (TI-M) berkata perjanjian konsesi baharu bagi kutipan fi mesti merangkumi perlindungan kontrak yang ketat bagi mengelakkan tunggakan hasil kerajaan dalam jumlah besar.
Presidennya, Raymon Ram, berkata kutipan hasil pada masa depan perlu dibayar terus ke akaun kerajaan, manakala bayaran kepada penyedia perkhidmatan dibuat secara berasingan oleh agensi berkaitan.

“Prinsip asasnya mudah. Penyedia perkhidmatan swasta boleh membantu mengutip hasil kerajaan, tetapi mereka tidak sepatutnya membiarkan sejumlah besar wang awam terkumpul di tangan mereka atau mempunyai kuasa budi bicara terhadap wang itu,” katanya kepada FMT.

“Kontrak perlu menetapkan pencetus penggantungan lebih awal supaya vendor tidak boleh terus mengumpul hasil kerajaan ketika notis peringatan dikeluarkan berulang kali,” kata Raymon sambil menambah bahawa kontrak konsesi pada masa depan perlu mempunyai mekanisme penguatkuasaan yang ketat.

Anak syarikat MYEG, Zetrix AI Bhd, mengumpul tunggakan sebanyak RM314 juta dalam bentuk fi cukai jalan dan saman trafik yang dikutip bagi pihak Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan (JPJ) tetapi belum diserahkan kepada kerajaan sejak Mei.

JPJ menggantung perkhidmatan kutipan syarikat itu pada 5 Okt selepas mengeluarkan 35 notis dan mengadakan empat sesi libat urus, yang akhirnya mendorong Zetrix AI mengemukakan cadangan penyelesaian kepada Putrajaya.

Menteri Pengangkutan Loke Siew Fook turut mendedahkan bahawa syarikat itu yang dahulunya dikenali sebagai MyEG Services Bhd, telah menyerahkan cek bernilai RM231 juta, tetapi pihak bank kemudian memaklumkan bahawa ia menerima arahan daripada Zetrix supaya pembayaran itu tidak diproses.

Raymon mengkritik kelewatan selama lima bulan sebelum tindakan tegas diambil terhadap Zetrix, dengan berkata sekadar mengeluarkan notis berulang kali ketika tunggakan terus meningkat bukanlah mekanisme kawalan yang berkesan.
“35 notis peringatan tidak boleh dianggap sebagai mekanisme kawalan yang memadai apabila ratusan juta ringgit hasil kerajaan terlibat,” katanya.
Beliau menggesa Putrajaya melaksanakan audit forensik bebas bagi menetapkan kronologi kejadian dengan jelas, bermula daripada kegagalan pertama menyerahkan kutipan kepada kerajaan.

“Pihak yang bertanggungjawab juga perlu dikenal pasti sepanjang rantaian pembuat keputusan dan tidak seharusnya terhad kepada pegawai bawahan, sekiranya pegawai kanan mengetahui jumlah wang yang berisiko terus meningkat dan mempunyai kuasa untuk campur tangan.”

Pegawai penyelidikan kanan Pusat Memerangi Rasuah dan Kronisme (C4) Bryan Cheah pula mengingatkan supaya kakitangan kementerian tidak dipersalahkan secara terburu-buru, dengan mengambil kira notis yang dikeluarkan berulang kali serta cek yang gagal ditunaikan.
Bagaimanapun, Cheah berkata pihak berkuasa perlu menyiasat sama ada terdapat unsur rasuah di sebalik kegagalan menyerahkan wang kutipan itu kepada kerajaan.

“C4 menggesa kerajaan menilai semula dasar perolehan semasa bagi memastikan kontrak dan konsesi yang diberikan kepada pihak swasta mematuhi kod tatakelakuan yang ketat, termasuk protokol tindakan yang perlu diambil sekiranya berlaku ketidakpatuhan terhadap syarat kontrak.”

Beliau berkata matlamat utama pentadbiran awam yang baik ialah pengawasan bagi mencegah masalah daripada berlaku, sambil menegaskan bahawa tindakan menghukum hanya diambil selepas sesuatu kejadian berlaku.

“Secara asasnya, penalti ialah tindak balas terhadap keadaan apabila pelanggaran atau ketidakpatuhan terhadap syarat telah berlaku. Tadbir urus yang baik bertujuan memastikan perkara sedemikian tidak berlaku sejak awal lagi.”
46e2cce1230787f2: JERUSALEM: Israel's foreign minister on Friday accused Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas of "fooling the international community" by planning to postpone upcoming legislative polls, as indications of a delay multiply.

Abbas' Palestinian Authority (PA) has not yet officially announced a postponement of the elections, which are due to take place on Nov 28. But many Palestinians expect them to be delayed or cancelled, as happened in 2021.
"Mahmoud Abbas is fooling the international community by cancelling once again promised elections," Israeli foreign minister Gideon Saar wrote on X.
"They keep deceiving. Consequences? Not for the corrupt PA!" he added.

The last legislative elections in the Palestinian territories were held two decades ago, and holding polls is part of the reforms demanded by the international community, including the European Union.

Palestinian factions including Abbas' Fatah and its rival Hamas have agreed to hold a "national dialogue" before legislative elections in November, with a source telling AFP on Thursday that the factions were seeking to postpone the vote.

Citing a PA source earlier in October, Palestinian official news agency Wafa reported that Israel had refused to allow Palestinian election officials access to east Jerusalem or Gaza ahead of the polls, increasing concerns that the vote will be postponed.
In early September, top Palestinian official Jibril Rajoub told reporters the November elections would not be held on time.
Rajoub, secretary-general of Fatah, said holding presidential elections first "would solve a large part of the problem".
The last legislative elections in the Palestinian territories were held in 2006, when Islamist movement Hamas won. They defeated Fatah, which dominates the Palestinian Authority.
The ensuring rift set off a round of factional fighting, with Hamas later seizing power in the Gaza Strip and creating a territorial divide between Fatah in the West Bank and Hamas in Gaza.
As a result, the Palestinian Legislative Council, which is the PA's parliament, has not met since 2007.
Abbas won the last Palestinian presidential election in 2005, and his term should have expired in 2009, but he has since ruled by decree.
In June, the 90-year-old leader signed a decree providing for a presidential election to be held at the beginning of 2027.

175ad4ef7e406c5a: KUALA LUMPUR: The deaths of two students in separate incidents in Johor and Pahang were among the major crime cases reported by the New Straits Times this week.

In Yong Peng, 16-year-old student Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal was found dead at her school on Oct 3, while in Kuantan, a 19-year-old student, Elisa Jonova Masilamani, was found dead at a house on Oct 6 following an alleged argument with her boyfriend.
Below are some of the crimes reported this week.
FORM FOUR STUDENT FOUND DEAD AT JOHOR SCHOOL
Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16, was found dead at a secondary school in Yong Peng, Batu Pahat, on Oct 3.
Her grandmother found her covered in blood at the school's hall after realising that she had not returned home by about 5.30pm.
Police arrested three 16-year-old boys on the same day, with one remanded for six days until Oct 9.
Federal police Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said a post-mortem confirmed that Irene died from blunt force trauma to the head.
The case is being investigated for murder.
19-YEAR-OLD STUDENT STRANGLED TO DEATH IN KUANTAN
In Kuantan, Elisa Jonova Masilamani, a 19-year-old student was found dead at a house in Air Putih on Oct 6 following an argument with her boyfriend.
The boyfriend, also 19, contacted the police.
Police were immediately dispatched to the rented house along Jalan Air Putih 2 where they found Elisa Jonova lying unconscious on a bed inside a rented room on the ground floor.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the boyfriend was believed to be unhappy that the victim had met another man.
A post-mortem confirmed that Elisa Jonova died from strangulation.
The suspect has been remanded for seven days until Oct 12, with the case being investigated for murder.
DRAMA AT SUBANG AIRPORT AS FOUR NABBED
Enforcement teams swooped on a private jet at a Subang Airport hangar on Wednesday where they arrested four people moments before the aircraft was due to take off for Manila.
This was a follow-up operation as investigations widened into the recent case where Laos authorities uncovered an attempt to smuggle 521kg of crystal methamphetamine.
Among the four who were arrested on Wednesday was a Malaysian pilot.

The operator of the private jet, CGT Asia Limited, has denied any wrongdoing after one of its aircraft was linked to an attempted trafficking of 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from Laos to the Philippines.

The company also confirmed that its director and three crew members, who were detained at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang on Wednesdayh were released the same day after giving their statements to the Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID).

It was reported that they were preparing to take off when enforcement personnel moved in. It was learnt the aircraft was configured for medical evacuation operations and equipped with medical equipment.
The flight was understood to have been scheduled to fly to Manila to pick up a patient before transporting the patient to Japan.

This was believed to be a follow-up operation to the incident on Oct 1 when a private jet that left Subang for Laos later became the focus of a major drug investigation after authorities seized 521kg of crystal methamphetamine at the Luang Prabang International Airport.
Police later confirmed that the co-pilot on that flight was a Malaysian. He was among 13 people arrested in Laos.
POLICEMEN DENY TOUTING CLAIMS IN MCBA CHIEF CASE

The two Special Branch policemen allegedly assaulted by Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain at KLIA Terminal 1 on Sept 28 broke their silence on Wednesday when they denied claims that they were acting as touts or involved in "counter setting".
Speaking through their lawyers, Lance Corporals Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman and Mohammad Faiz Muhamad, said they were carrying out official duties when the alleged incident occurred.

Their lawyers said any allegation that the policemen were acting as touts or involved in counter setting should be supported by evidence and should not be used to divert attention from the alleged assault.
The two were allegedly physically assaulted by Shuhaily in a public area, causing injuries and affecting their dignity as civil servants.
Police, meanwhile, said, they have recorded statements from 25 witnesses and obtained CCTV footage and a medical report.
The incident came to light after a video showing Shuhaily berating two men went viral, with one of them appearing to have been grabbed forcefully by the ears.
Shuhaily later said he was prepared to be investigated over the incident.

1034abccea401f25: KUALA LUMPUR: An e-hailing driver has pleaded not guilty to three charges over a crash that killed a 22-year-old Maldivian student and injured another passenger, including driving under the influence of methamphetamine.

The case leads this week's Court Watch, alongside murder charges against two teenagers over the death of their junior, fresh developments in the Zara Qairina inquest, and several significant legal challenges.
E-hailing driver charged over crash that killed student, injured another

Five days after a crash claimed the life of a 22-year-old Maldivian student, an e-hailing driver was brought before the Shah Alam Magistrate's Court to face three charges linked to the accident, including causing death while driving under the influence of methamphetamine.

Muhamad Syafiq Ibrahim, 37, pleaded not guilty to a charge of driving a Perodua Ativa under the influence of methamphetamine, resulting in the death of Aamina Imeely Nazim, a private university student.
He also claimed trial to a second charge of driving the same vehicle under the influence of the drug, causing injuries to another 22-year-old Maldivian passenger, Aishath Sara Nizam.
Syafiq further pleaded not guilty to a third charge of driving without due care and attention, resulting in a collision with another vehicle and causing injuries to Aishath.
Aamina and Aishath were passengers in Syafiq's e-hailing vehicle.
The offences were allegedly committed at 8.40pm on Oct 4 along the Damansara-Puchong Highway, near the Puchong Selatan toll plaza, heading towards Puchong.
Police said the crash occurred when Syafiq's Ativa crashed into another car while approaching the toll plaza's RFID lane.
The impact caused the Ativa to spin before overturning.
Below are some of the other major court cases this week.
TWO TEENAGERS CHARGED WITH THE MURDER OF THEIR JUNIOR
In Kuala Pilah, two 16-year-old boys were charged with murdering their 14-year-old junior at a sports school hostel last month.
They were charged with murdering Muhammad Idlan Fareeq Shahril between 7.30pm and 8.50pm on Sept 25.
The proceedings, led by Negri Sembilan prosecution director Engku Ahmad Rashdi Engku Abdillah, were conducted in camera as both accused are juveniles.
Lawyer Datuk Hanif Hassan, who represented both teenagers, said the court had fixed Dec 7 for the submission of pathology, chemistry and forensic reports.
He said the defence had applied for both teenagers to be sent to a correctional centre pending the next court date to allow counselling by the Social Welfare Department.
CORONER'S COURT VISITS ZARA QAIRINA'S SCHOOL AGAIN
From the courtroom to SMKA Tun Datu Mustapha, the Coroner's Court returned to the school in Papar for a second site visit as part of the inquest into the death of 13-year-old Zara Qairina Mahathir.

The latest visit on Oct 5 lasted nearly four hours, with coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan, deputy public prosecutors and legal representatives of interested parties inspecting classrooms, the design and technology room, hostel dormitories and toilets.
Teachers and students familiar with the school also accompanied the group and helped clarify locations, layout and physical conditions referred to during the inquest.
The first site visit was conducted on Sept 11 last year.
Zara Qairina was found unconscious near a drain at her school hostel about 4am on July 16 last year and was pronounced dead the following day at Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
This week, Zara Qairina's half-sister, Malianah Mahathir, 25, and mother, Noraidah Lamat, 46, testified as the 81st and 82nd witnesses respectively.
UNDANGS WITHDRAW JUDICIAL REVIEW AFTER MB SIGNS PROCLAMATION
A legal challenge by the Undang Yang Empat came to an end after Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim signed the proclamation they had sought to compel him to sign.

The four Undangs had filed a judicial review application seeking an order requiring Ismail to sign the proclamation concerning the removal of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
However, Ismail signed the proclamation on Aug 3, before the court could hear the substantive challenge.
Lawyer Mohd Khairul Azam Aziz told High Court judge Norliza Othman that the application had become academic.
Norliza allowed the withdrawal without liberty for the applicants to file afresh and ordered them to pay RM40,000 in costs to four proposed interveners.
The four Undangs are Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, Datuk Muhammed Abdullah and Datuk Abd Rahim Yasin.
BAR FAILS TO CHALLENGE TERRIRUDIN'S JAC APPOINTMENT
The Malaysian Bar failed in its bid to challenge the appointment of Federal Court judge Tan Sri Ahmad Terrirudin Mohd Salleh to the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC).
High Court judge Norliza Othman dismissed the Bar's application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings, ruling that the proposed challenge was not legally arguable.

She said Section 5(1)(e) of the Judicial Appointments Commission Act 2009 was clear in requiring the appointee to be a serving Federal Court judge and the appointment to be made by the prime minister.
The court found that both requirements were met in Ahmad Terrirudin's appointment.
The Bar had sought a certiorari order to quash Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's decision to appoint Ahmad Terrirudin as a member of the JAC.

43240a8a2f5ccab0: WASHINGTON: US treasury secretary Scott Bessent will not attend the IMF and World Bank's annual meetings in Bangkok next week, a department official confirmed Friday, as domestic pressures grow over war with Iran and bond yields remain elevated.
Bessent was expected to chair a meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bank governors on Thursday, with the United States holding the rotating presidency of the grouping.
But the treasury department said that deputy treasury secretary Francis Brooke and under secretary for international affairs Erin Browne will instead lead the US delegation.
A US official added that Bessent has "domestic engagements," without providing further details.
The annual meetings, held outside the International Monterary Fund's Washington headquarters once every three years, come weeks before key US midterm elections this time.
President Donald Trump's Republican Party will be trying to retain control of Congress in the November vote, amid growing voter worries over affordability.

Americans are feeling the squeeze from rising energy costs following war in the Middle East, which erupted after US-Israel strikes from late February that targeted Iran. Tehran has since choked off the Strait of Hormuz, sending oil prices rocketing.
Bessent also did not travel to Cape Town for a G20 meeting last year.
His predecessors Janet Yellen and Steven Mnuchin previously attended the IMF's annual meetings in Marrakech and Bali respectively.

US officials will work with partners in Bangkok to address "policies and structural imbalances that have held back growth and contributed to persistent global imbalances," the treasury department said.
Officials will also seek "greater transparency and more effective approaches to sovereign debt," the agency added.
6dae77923709c840: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled Budget 2027 yesterday, the fifth by his administration, appearing to shift greater focus towards ensuring that ordinary Malaysians benefit from economic growth and reforms pursued over the past four years.

The national budget totalling RM510 billion, up from RM470 billion in Budget 2026, was tabled amid elevated global fuel prices and Malaysia’s ageing population, and could be the final one before the 16th General Election (GE16).

After years of focusing on economic stability, fiscal discipline and reforms, Budget 2027 appears to place greater emphasis on ensuring that the gains from these efforts are felt by ordinary Malaysians in their daily lives, with living costs still pinching households.
To this end, Anwar has sought to boost household incomes through higher wages and cash aid, more support for businesses and stronger safety nets through tax reliefs and incentives in Budget 2027.
Reforms remain high on his administration’s agenda, with Anwar promising further measures to tighten oversight of government procurement and the management of public funds in 2027.
Here’s a snapshot of what makes Budget 2027:
Cash assistance and cost of living
The government will increase the allocation for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to RM16 billion, from RM15 billion.
STR recipients: All recipients will receive SARA of up to RM150 a month, or RM1,800 a year, benefiting up to nine million people.
Other adults: Malaysians aged 18 and above who are not STR recipients will receive Sara Madani of RM100 twice in 2027 — before Aidilfitri and ahead of the 70th anniversary of Merdeka.
Cheaper groceries: Fresh produce will be offered at prices up to 30 per cent lower at Jualan Rahmah Madani and Agro Madani sales
Rural supplies: RM250 million will be allocated to expand the distribution of essential goods to rural and interior areas, including six new locations.
Tax relief and take-home pay
Individual income tax relief will increase from RM9,000 to RM12,000, while tax rates will be lowered by one percentage point for selected income brackets.
The tax rate for income between RM70,000 and RM100,000 will fall to 18 per cent.
The rate for income between RM100,000 and RM150,000 will fall to 24 per cent.
The tax rate for income above RM1 million will be set at 30 per cent.
The government expects the changes to increase disposable income by up to RM1,600 for about five million taxpayers.

Tax relief will also be expanded to cover postnatal care, care expenses for parents and grandparents, sports shoes, tuition for children, subscriptions to artificial intelligence services, vaccinations and adoption costs for pets from registered centres.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Members of the public watching the live telecast of 2027 Budget by Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar in Parliament around Putrajaya Oct 9, 2026. — Picture by Choo Choy May.
Workers, minimum wage and gig workers
The minimum wage will increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month from June 2027, affecting more than four million workers.
Small and medium enterprises with annual sales below RM50 million will be given time to adjust their business models.
The government also announced a starting minimum wage of RM2,500 a month for semi-skilled occupations and graduates.
Government-linked investment companies and government-linked companies will raise their living-wage benchmark from RM3,100 to RM3,400 a month, benefiting about 230,000 workers.
For e-hailing and p-hailing workers, the government and Grab will jointly fund a RM160 million package from 2027 to improve net income and welfare.

This package is expected to increase median-level e-hailing drivers’ net income by up to RM227 a month and p-hailing riders’ income by up to RM100 a month. It also includes matching contributions to Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) schemes, with the government’s contribution rising from 35 per cent to 50 per cent if platform companies also contribute.
E-hailing and p-hailing workers will also be eligible for Employees Provident Fund (EPF) matching contributions of up to RM600 a year or RM6,000 over their lifetime.
All Malaysian citizens will also be registered automatically as EPF members when they turn 18.
Students and families
The government will increase several forms of education assistance and expand support for students.
School aid: Bantuan Awal Persekolahan or early schooling assistance will increase from RM150 to RM200 per pupil. A family with four school-going children will receive RM800.
University travel: FlySiswa Madani air-ticket assistance will increase from RM400 to RM500 for more than 60,000 public university students.
Form Six: Students will receive a living allowance of RM2,500, matching the allowance for matriculation students and benefiting about 90,000 students.

PTPTN loans: Borrowers earning RM2,500 or less a month can defer repayments in 2027. Those earning between RM2,500 and RM3,000 will pay a minimum of RM50 a month. Borrowers without arrears who repay regularly will receive a 10 per cent discount.
Affordable meals: Dapur Siswa Madani will be extended to polytechnics and teacher education institutes, with RM20 million for cooking equipment, food contributions and RM5 meals.

Student housing: The first phase of Universiti Malaya’s student residence is scheduled for completion in 2031, benefiting 10,000 students. The Retirement Fund Inc (KWAP) will invest RM750 million in Vista Kampus housing at six universities, including UniSZA and UiTM.
The government will also allocate RM800 million for higher education infrastructure, including lecture rooms, student residences and replacement of ageing equipment.
Schools, hospitals and public services
Education and healthcare remain among the largest areas of federal spending.

The Education Ministry will receive nearly RM69 billion, up from RM66.2 billion this year, Health Ministry will receive RM47.7 billion, the Higher Education Ministry will get RM19.1 billion and the Home Affairs and Defence ministries will each receive RM22 billion.

For schools, the allocation to repair and maintain all types of schools will double from RM1 billion to RM2 billion — am allocation that includes repairs for national schools, Chinese national-type schools, Tamil national-type schools and registered rakyat religious schools, tahfiz institutions and pondok schools.
A further RM1.3 billion will be provided to upgrade 682 dilapidated schools, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak.
The government also expects 3,500 additional classrooms to be completed by the end of this year to accommodate more Year One pupils.

For public healthcare, RM1.2 billion will be allocated to maintain and repair hospitals and clinics, while more than RM770 million will go towards modern medical equipment, including 400 new ambulances and upgraded haemodialysis facilities.

Nine new healthcare facilities will be built, including a specialist complex and day-treatment centre at Hospital Sultanah Aminah in Johor, a specialist dental centre in Kuching, and integrated health complexes in Gerik, Perak, and Rembau, Negeri Sembilan.

More than 9,000 contract doctors will be made permanent medical officers at public healthcare facilities next year. Paramedics and nurses will receive RM200 post-basic incentives monthly while Air Health Service staff will receive RM100 monthly.
The government will also introduce the MediAsas affordable medical plan in January 2027.
EPF members aged below 55 can pay their premiums using their Akaun Sejahera.
Meanwhile, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) with fewer than 75 employees will receive a first-year premium subsidy of RM200 per worker, capped at 50 workers per company.
The scheme is expected to benefit up to 200,000 workers.

PeKa B40 will continue offering free health screenings, medical equipment assistance and cancer-treatment incentives for STR recipients and their spouses aged 40 and above, with RM80 million allocated.
MySalam will also continue, while the Medical Aid Fund will increase from RM40 million to RM60 million.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The government expects the changes to increase disposable income by up to RM1,600 for about five million taxpayers. — Picture by Choo Choy May.
Help for senior citizens and people with disabilities
Welfare assistance for senior citizens will receive RM1.3 billion, benefiting nearly 200,000 recipients.

The monthly allowance for caring for bedridden people with disabilities and the chronically ill will increase from RM500 to RM600, while the income threshold for the disabled workers’ allowance will increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000.

Anwar also reduced the service tax rate for elderly care services from eight to six per cent, with a full exemption on fees up to RM96,000 annually. Some 8,000 caregivers will also be trained through an allocation of RM40 million under HRD Corp.
Pupils with special educational needs will also receive a higher allowance of RM200, while the teaching incentive for special education teachers will increase from RM250 to RM300 a month.

Two new Permata Kurnia centres — a Malaysian early intervention and education programme for children with autism — will be built in Melaka and Pahang, alongside more than 130 new Tabika Tunas Istimewa classes in rural areas.
Public transport and connectivity
Public transport users will benefit from continued subsidised passes and investments to improve services.
My50: The pass will continue for 300,000 Prasarana bus and rail users in the Klang Valley.
MyKomuter50: A new pass will benefit 40,000 KTM Komuter users, with average savings of up to RM160 a month.
Free passes: About 360,000 school pupils, people with disabilities and children below six will receive free passes.
Train services: The government will acquire 42 new train sets for ETS and KTM Komuter services. Prasarana will invest more than RM3.4 billion in a comprehensive rail-service recovery programme.
Bus services: RM270 million will be allocated to improve bus services in major cities, including links to 15 East Coast stations ahead of the East Coast Rail Link’s operation.

The first phase of the ECRL, from Kota Bharu to the Gombak Integrated Transport Terminal, is expected to begin operating in December 2026, while a bus station will also be built at the Kota Bharu ECRL station.
Roads, water, electricity and internet
Rural communities will receive RM3.3 billion for basic infrastructure, including roads, community facilities, clean water and electricity. The allocation for rural roads will rise to RM2.3 billion.
The National Non-Revenue Water programme will receive RM2.5 billion to replace 1,900km of ageing critical pipes.

Under the Jendela connectivity initiative, the government plans to extend 4G coverage to all Orang Asli villages, improve internet connectivity along 7,000km of roads and 1,700km of railway lines, and implement the Madani Undersea Cable project.
Road projects in Sabah and Sarawak will receive RM3.3 billion, while another RM350 million will be set aside for federal road maintenance by small contractors in both states.
Sabah will receive RM18.7 billion in federal allocation, up from RM17.6 billion this year, while Sarawak will receive RM16.2 billion, up from RM15.1 billion.
In Sabah, RM204 million will be spent on installing STATCOM systems at the Dam Road and Segaliud substations, while the Southern Link transmission line project will continue.
The federal government will also provide RM600 million to ensure electricity supply continuity in Sabah.
Flood protection and disaster aid
Flood mitigation projects will continue in Kuching, Sarawak, while the second phase of Sungai Golok in Kelantan and Sungai Kemaman in Terengganu.
